A.  RECOGNITION

  1. The Air Line Pilots Association, International, has furnished to the Company evidence that a
  majority of the pilots employed by the Company have designated the Association to represent them
  and in their behalf negotiate and conclude an Agreement with the Company as to hours of labor,
  wages and other employment conditions covering the pilots in the employ of the Company in
  accordance with the provisions of Title II of the Railway Labor Act, as amended.

  2. The Company recognizes the right of pilots on the Pilots’ System Seniority List to perform the
  Company's flying and operate the Company's aircraft as specified in this Agreement.

B. SCOPE

  1. This Agreement covers all revenue flying performed by or for the Company or any Affiliate.

  2. As used herein, the term "all revenue flying performed by or for the Company or any Affiliate" shall
  include, but not be limited to, all flying over the Company's or any Affiliate's present or future routes
  and extensions thereof, and any contract (government, military or commercial) flying, charter flying
  and flying subcontracted for or by the Company or any Affiliate and/or subcontracted out by the
  Company or any Affiliate, any "wet-lease" flying, and any flying under the Company's or an
  Affiliate's control.

  3. Except as provided in Paragraph B6 and B.7 of this Section, all revenue flying by or for the
  Company or any Affiliate covered by this Agreement shall be performed by pilots whose names
  appear on the Hawaiian Airlines, Inc. Pilots’ System Seniority List under the terms and conditions of
  the Agreement.

  4. No revenue flying covered by this Agreement shall be performed by the Company or an Affiliate
  until the Company and the Association have signed an agreement covering the rates of pay, rules and
  working conditions applicable to such flying.

  5. In the event that the Company or an Affiliate determines to perform revenue flying which is not
  already covered by this Agreement, the following procedures will be followed:

  a. The Company will send written notification to the Chairman of the Hawaiian Airlines Pilots'
  Master Executive Council of its intent to commence such revenue flying. At the same time, a
  copy of such notification will be sent to the President of the Association and to The Air Line
  Pilots Association Contract Administration Office that is then supporting the HAL MEC
  (currently, the ALPA SEA Contract Administration Office, 18000 International Boulevard, Suite
  300, Seattle, WA 98188).

  b. Within two (2) consecutive calendar days of such notification, the parties will commence
  conferences in the Company's general offices in Honolulu, Hawaii or at some other mutually
  agreeable location. Such conferences shall be for the purpose of negotiating the rates of pay,
  rules and working conditions applicable to such revenue flying. Direct conferences between the
  parties shall continue for not more than ten (10) consecutive calendar days or until an agreement
  is reached, whichever occurs first, unless the parties mutually extend such ten (10) day period.

  c. If no agreement has been reached at the end of such ten (10) day period or any extension thereof,
  then the open unresolved issues will be submitted promptly for determination by an arbitrator to

be mutually agreed upon by the parties. The arbitrator shall have the authority and responsibility
  to hear and determine all of the open unresolved issues.

  d. The hearing before the arbitrator will commence as soon as possible after the ten (10) day period
  of direct negotiation or any extension thereof. Within ten (10) consecutive calendar days after
  the close of the hearing, the arbitrator shall furnish each of the parties with a copy of their written
  decision concerning the open unresolved items and such decision shall be final and binding upon
  the parties hereto.

  e. The entire period from notification specified in Subparagraph (a) above until the arbitrator issues
  their written decision shall include not more than thirty (30) consecutive calendar days, unless
  mutually extended by the parties hereto.

  6. Paragraph B.3. of this Section shall prohibit the Company or an Affiliate of the Company from
  entering into marketing and related arrangements that permit another air carrier to utilize the
  Company’s designator code, name, logo, marks or cargo manifests in commercial flight operations
  (any such agreement, a “Code Sharing Agreement”), unless the requirements of either this
  Paragraph B.6 or of Paragraph B.7 of this Section are satisfied. Paragraph B.3 of this Section shall
  also prohibit the Company from partly or wholly acquiring, establishing, Controlling, or operating
  another carrier that does not operate under this Agreement, unless the Company ensures that the
  requirements of this Paragraph B.6 are satisfied with respect to such carrier and that it operates for
  Hawaiian as a Feeder Carrier.

  a. This Paragraph B.6 governs “Feeder Carriers,” and Paragraph B.7 of this Section 1 governs
  “Code Share Partners.” The term “Feeder Carrier” refers to an air carrier, whether or not partly
  or wholly owned, Controlled, or operated by the Company or an Affiliate of the Company, that
  operates under a Code Sharing Agreement using its own operating certificate in lawfully
  operable commercial flight operations under the following conditions in this Paragraph B.6. The
  term “Code Share Partner” refers to an air carrier that is not partly or wholly owned, controlled,
  or operated by the Company or an Affiliate of the Company and operates using such carrier’s
  operating certificate, under the conditions in Paragraph B.7 of this Section.

  b. A Feeder Carrier acquired, established or operated by the Company, or the portion of a Feeder
  Carrier operated under a Code Sharing Agreement with the Company, may operate only within
  the Hawaiian Islands (but not to or from Hawaii).

  c. A Feeder Carrier acquired, established or operated by the Company, and the portion of a Feeder
  Carrier operated under a Code Sharing Agreement with the Company, may operate only
  turboprop aircraft, and such aircraft must be lawfully operable in commercial flight operations
  with a maximum certificated seating capacity of sixty-nine (69) seats and a maximum
  certificated gross takeoff weight of no more than 69,000 pounds in passenger operations, or a
  maximum certificated gross takeoff weight of no more than 69,000 pounds in all-freight
  operations.

  d. With respect to Inter-Island Feeder Carriers:

  1) An Inter-Island Feeder Carrier will conduct no commercial passenger flight operations of
  any kind on the following city pairs: HNL-LIH, HNL-ITO, HNL-KOA, and HNL-OGG.

  2) Feeder Carriers all freight aircraft may not operate an aggregate of more than the greater of
  the number of available ton miles operated by the largest air cargo carrier in the Inter-Island

Hawaii market (“Largest Air Cargo Carrier”) in the twelve months preceding the January
  14th, 2010 or the available ton miles then currently operated by the Largest Air Cargo
  Carrier.

  3) The Company will neither furlough any Hawaiian pilots nor reduce the number of block
  hours the Company operates in 717 or equivalent jet operations within the Hawaiian Islands
  as a result of initiation or expansion of flying by an Inter-Island Feeder Carrier. The
  existence of an Inter-Island Feeder Carrier will not by itself be sufficient to demonstrate
  causation.

  4) During any consecutive twelve-month period of Inter-Island Feeder Carrier operation ending
  on the last day of any calendar month following the effective date of this Agreement, the
  Company will not operate fewer than twenty-nine thousand (29,000) hours of Inter-Island
  turbojet block hours measured over the same period.

  e. The Company shall not be required to apply this Agreement to pilots employed by a Feeder
  Carrier, and the Association shall make no argument to or in any forum that application of this
  Agreement to the Feeder Carrier is required by contract or law.

  f.  If the Company establishes a Feeder Carrier, or if it acquires a Feeder Carrier whose pilots are
  not represented by a union, the Company agrees to recognize, or cause the Feeder Carrier to
  recognize, the Association as the representative of such pilots upon a lawful demonstration of
  majority support and will take a neutral position with respect to the Association’s efforts to
  secure and provide that lawful demonstration.

  g. The Company will make commercially reasonable efforts to obtain the same jumpseat and pass
  privileges on the aircraft operated by the Feeder Carrier as Hawaiian pilots have on Hawaiian
  aircraft.

  h. If the Company chooses to acquire and operate turboprop aircraft on Hawaiian’s certificate, then
  the Parties shall meet to negotiate the rates of pay, rules and working conditions for such aircraft
  pursuant to Section 26.I, and if no agreement is reached within ninety (90) days, the rates of pay,
  rules and working conditions for such aircraft shall be determined through Expedited Arbitration
  pursuant to Section 1.I and according to prevailing industry standards, with each party in such
  Expedited Arbitration having the right to strike one industry comparable carrier from the Board’s
  consideration.

  i.  The Company will require Feeder Carriers that it wholly owns and operates to provide a right of
  first interview and hire to furloughed Hawaiian pilots and will use its commercially reasonable
  best efforts to secure such rights from Feeder Carriers that it partly owns or which operate under
  a Code Sharing Agreement.

  7. Except as expressly permitted in Paragraph B6 of this Section 1, and in this Paragraph B.7, the
  Company shall not permit any other carrier to utilize the Company’s designator code, name, trade
  name, brand, logo, trademarks, service marks, aircraft livery or aircraft paint scheme without the
  express written consent of the Association in commercial flight operations. The following provisions
  of this Paragraph B.7 apply to “Code Share Partners,” defined as air carriers, other than Feeder
  Carriers, that are not partly or wholly owned, Controlled, or operated by the Company or an Affiliate
  of the Company, and that operate under a Code Sharing Agreement with the Company.

a. The Company may permit a passenger to book under the HA or HA* code an itinerary that
  includes a nonstop flight operated by a Code Share Partner that is a Domestic Air Carrier subject
  to the following limitations:

  1) if and only if the flight does not operate between an airport in Hawaii and an airport in the
  remainder of the United States or, if it is not a Feeder Carrier, between airports in Hawaii;

  2) if the flight operates between an airport in Hawaii and a country outside the United States,
  only if during each calendar quarter the available seat miles scheduled to be operated by the
  Domestic Air Carrier under the HA or HA* code to or from Hawaii and the country outside
  the United States do not exceed one-third (1/3) of the available seat miles scheduled to be
  operated by the Company to or from Hawaii and such country.

  b. The Company may permit a passenger to book under the HA or HA* code an itinerary that
  includes a nonstop flight operated by a Code Share Partner that is a Foreign Air Carrier only if
  either (i) the flight does not operate to or from Hawaii, or (ii) it operates between a point in that
  Code Share Partner’s home country and Honolulu or another Company Connecting Airport
  subject to the limitations of subparagraph 7.c.

  c. For each Foreign Air Carrier that becomes a Code Share Partner after the effective date of this
  Agreement, and for each Foreign Air Carrier that is a Code Share Partner as of the effective date
  of this Agreement, for each calendar quarter the Current ASM Ratio for flights scheduled to be
  operated between that Code Share Partner’s home country and Hawaii will not exceed 110% of
  the Base ASM Ratio for that quarter for such flights.

  1) For purposes of this subparagraph 7.c., the “Base ASM Ratio” for a Foreign Air Carrier that
  is a Code Share Partner means the ratio in a Base Calendar Quarter between (i) a numerator
  equal to the greater of (a) available seat miles scheduled to be operated in the relevant period
  by the Foreign Air Carrier on nonstop flights to or from Hawaii and the relevant home

  The following definitions shall apply to the capitalized terms in this Section 1 of the Agreement:

  1. Agreement. The term "Agreement" means and includes this collective bargaining agreement
  between the Association and the Company and any and all other agreements between the Association
  and the Company or among the Association, the Company and its Affiliates.

  2. Entity. The term "Entity" shall mean any business form of any kind, including without limitation any
  natural person, corporation, company, unincorporated association, division, partnership, trustee, trust,
  receivership, joint venture, administrator or executor.

  3. Control. Entity A shall be deemed to "Control" Entity B if Entity A, whether directly or indirectly,
  (a) maintains the power, right, or authority to manage or direct the management of Entity B's
  operations, or (b) maintains the power, right or authority to appoint a majority of Entity B's Board of
  Directors or similar governing body, or (c) maintains the power, right or authority to appoint a
  minority of B's Board of Directors or similar governing body, if such minority maintains the power,
  right or authority to appoint or remove any of B's executive officers, to approve a substantial part of
  B's business or operating plans or to approve a substantial part of B's debt or equity offerings, or (d)
  owns securities that constitute, are exercisable for or are exchangeable into forty percent (40%) or
  more of Entity B's outstanding common stock or otherwise owns forty percent (40%) or more of
  Entity B.

  4. Common Control. A shall be deemed to be under "Common Control" with B if any third person or
  entity Controls both A and B whether directly or indirectly through the Control of other persons or
  entities that Control A and B.

  5. Parent. As used in the Agreement, the term "Parent" refers to any Entity that Controls the Company,
  whether directly or indirectly through the Control of other Entities that Control the Company.

  6. Affiliates. As used in the Agreement, the term "Affiliate" refers to (i) any Parent, (ii) any Entity that
  Controls or manages the Company or any Entity that the Company Controls or manages, or (iii) any
  Entity under Common Control with the Company, or (iv) any other corporate subsidiary, parent
  or division of the Company, a Parent or any other Affiliate.

  7. Domestic Air Carrier. As used in this Agreement, the term “Domestic Air Carrier” means an “air
  carrier” as defined in 49 U.S.C. Section 40102(a)(2) holding an air carrier certificate issued by the
  Administrator of the FAA under 14 C.F.R. Section 119.5.

  8. Foreign Air Carrier. As used in this Agreement, the term “Foreign Air Carrier” means a “foreign air
  carrier” as defined in 49 U.S.C. Section 40102(a)(21).

  means one that is offered for sale to the public via the OAG and similar services.

F. PROFIT BONUS PLAN

  1. Performance Bonus

  a. Each year, the Company will establish performance goals for on-time performance, safety,
  etc. Based on the yearly goals, quarterly goals will be set. These performance goals will be
  discussed with all unions and brought to the attention of all employees. For each quarter that
  the performance goals are met, each active full-time employee will receive a bonus of $150, a
  potential total of $600 per year, and each active part-time employee will be eligible for a
  quarterly bonus of $75 per quarter, a potential total of $300 per year. Any bonus payments
  will be reduced by applicable taxes and court required deductions. If goals are not met, no
  Performance Bonus will be paid for that quarter. Performance Bonus payments will be paid
  regardless of Company profitability. Should the Performance Bonus payments be increased
  for any other group, such increase shall not result in a decrease to ALPA’s share of any Profit
  Bonus.

  2. Profit Bonus

  a. The total potential Profit Bonus will be 5% of annual pretax profits (excluding extraordinary
  items and charges) from the first dollar of profit. Before being allocated among employee
  groups, the total potential Profit Bonus will be reduced dollar-for-dollar by the performance
  bonuses and any special bonuses paid for the year, excluding any payment under the
  Incentive Compensation Program. The Company may, at its discretion, pay the Profit Bonus
  on a quarterly, rather than an annual basis. Should any other group(s) be provided a different
  Profit Bonus formula, such group(s) will be separated into a different Profit Bonus plan so as
  not to negatively impact the ALPA share of this plan.

  b. The net Profit Bonus will first be divided among all employee groups (ALPA, AFA, IAM,
  non-represented, etc.) on the basis of each group’s pro rata share of W-2 wages for the year.
  The pro rata share of any non-participating employee group will not be paid out to any group.
  Within each participating group, the bonus will then be allocated based on regular W-2 wages
  (as defined below) of each eligible member of the group, or another basis if that is agreed
  upon. Profit Bonuses paid will be less applicable taxes and pretax deferral deductions. The
  Company would have discretion to set a minimum amount payable to any individual.

  Example:
  If Hawaiian’s 2009 pre-tax profit were $40 million the total potential bonus payment would
  be $2 million. If the Performance Bonuses paid out for the year totaled $600 thousand, then
  up to $1.4 million would be allocated among employee groups and individual employees in
  the manner described above.

  3. Incentive Compensation Program

  a. ALPA will participate in the Incentive Compensation Program established by the Board of
  Directors for senior management, with a target payout bonus of one (1) percent of W-2
  wages. The same numerical calculations established by the Board that determine the

  zero (0) percent to two (2) percent of the previous year's W-2 wages. Payment from the

E. POSTING REQUIREMENTS FOR PAY AND CREDIT TIME

  1.  The Company shall provide pilots with access to the pilots’ total time for pay purposes for each Duty
  Period. Such information/data shall reflect all Pay and Credit time and shall be a duplicate of the Pay
  and Credit time figures used by Crew Scheduling. Further, the information/data shall be made within
  two (2) days (unless unavailable due to technical/facilities outages or major issues (e.g., flood, power
  failure)) following the respective Duty Periods.

  2.  The following types of Pay and Credit shall be included in the daily posting of Pay and Credit:

  a.  Pay and Credit from the Captain’s flight report inclusive of Segment credits.

  b.  Pay and Credit for each Duty Period or credited block time, whichever is greater.

  c.  Pay and Credit for all paid absences from active line flying.

  d.  Pay and Credit for minimum report time.

  e.  Pay and Credit for Trip Rig.

  f.  Pay and Credit for training.

G. JURY DUTY

 1.  When a pilot is called for jury duty, they shall notify the Company immediately and the Company
  may request the court to release them from such jury duty, or the Company shall release them from
  all Company duties on such days they are called for selection or actively serve as a juror.

 2.  Total compensation to the pilot when called for selection or while actively serving on a jury shall
  equal that which they would normally have earned during such period less fees received for such
  services as follows:

  a.  A pilot awarded a Bid Run shall be Paid and Credited what they normally could have earned for
  any published Segments missed on their Monthly Run.

  b.  A pilot awarded a Reserve Run shall be Paid and Credited the greater of the following:
  1) Any published Segments missed as defined in Subparagraph 4.B.4; or
  2) For all work days missed on Jury Duty, five (5) hours per work day.

H. COMPANY BUSINESS

 1.  The Company Business period shall include all days performing Company Business, all travel days
  associated with such Company Business, and all days off within the Company Business period (e.g.,
  five (5) days of Company Business followed by two days off). Days off associated with Company
  Business count toward minimum days off provided they are at the pilot’s Domicile.

 2.  Except for the provisions of Section 8 (Administrative Pilots), if the Company requests a pilot
  perform service for the Company not directly related to their normal training or flight duties and such
  pilot accepts such assignment, then the pilot shall be Paid and Credited as follows:

  a.  Prior to the opening of the monthly bidding period:
  1) Five (5) hours of Pay and Credit per day during the company business period.
  2) During the company business period work days shall normally be five (5) work days
  followed by two (2) days off (Normally Monday through Friday work days and Saturday,
  Sunday and Company Holidays days off).
  3) Prorate days off pursuant to provisions of Section 26.II

  b.  After awarding of the Monthly Runs:
  1) Bid Run pilots Paid and Credited for Segments missed.
  2) Reserve Run pilots on Company business shall be Paid and Credited the greater of the
  following:
  a) For any published Segments missed as defined in Subparagraph B.4 of this Section; or
  b) For all workdays missed on Company business five (5) hours per workday.

A. HOURLY EXPENSE ALLOWANCE

  1. Pilots shall receive an hourly expense allowance to cover meals, laundry, and incidental expenses for
  each hour or portion thereof that a pilot is away from their Permanent Domicile. The hourly rate
  paid to pilots will be as follows:

  a. Interisland rate:
  1) At $2.00 per hour and prorated for fractions of an hour.
  2) Interisland as used herein shall mean “Interisland Flying” as defined in Subparagraph 2.A.35.

  b. International rate:
  1) At $2.50 per hour and prorated for fractions of an hour.
  2) Paid to any Interisland Pilot who departs the Hawaiian Islands for an overseas destination.
  3) International as used herein shall mean “International Flying” as defined in Subparagraph
  2.A.37.
  4) Paid for the entirety of any Mixed Flying grouping.

  2. The hourly expense allowance for an International Pilot voluntarily awarded a Flight Grouping at a
  Domicile other than their own shall begin one (1) hour prior to such pilot’s departure from their
  Domicile enroute for duty at another Domicile and end when such pilot is released from duty at their
  Domicile.

  3. If a pilot transits their Domicile during a Duty Period, their hourly allowance and Trip Rig will
  continue until such time as they are released from duty at their Permanent Domicile for the number
  of hours specified in Subsection 10.E (Rest Periods).

  4. A pilot, when on flying or ground training assignments at their Permanent Domicile, will receive
  each day the hourly allowance shown in Subparagraph 5.A.1, commencing when they are required to
  report for training (or when they actually report, whichever is later) and ending when they are
  released from training sessions that day. When training is conducted away from their Permanent
  Domicile, the pilot will receive the hourly allowance stipulated in Subparagraph 5.A.1 for that period
  of time beginning when the pilot departs their Permanent Domicile and ending when the pilot arrives
  back at their Permanent Domicile.

  5. The hourly expense allowance provided in Subparagraph 5.A.1 shall commence when a pilot departs
  their Permanent Domicile for temporary duty at another Permanent Domicile, or for duty at a
  Temporary Domicile, and shall continue until such time as the pilot returns to their Permanent
  Domicile after release from such duty. All pilots shall have a minimum of twenty-four (24) hours
  free of all duty immediately following transfer between Domiciles. If travel time is extended for
  personal reasons, it is understood that hourly expenses for this extended travel time will not be paid.
  A pilot shall not receive hourly expense allowance for days of vacation while serving at a Temporary
  Domicile.

  6. When a pilot’s scheduled Flight Grouping originates out of one airport and terminates at another
  airport serving their Domicile, the following “Transfer Times” will be used to increase the Duty
  Period, deadhead Pay and Credit time, and per diem due such pilot pursuant to Subparagraph 5.C.3:

  a. Airports  Transfer Times

  LAX-ONT  2.00 hours
  LAX-PMD  2.00 hours

B. LODGING

  1. In addition to the hourly expense allowances provided in Subsection 5.A (Hourly Expenses
  Allowance):

  a. The Company shall furnish suitable single room hotel accommodations (where available) in a
  suitable location for pilots:
  1) Scheduled to layover at a location for four (4) or more hours (Block In to Block Out); or
  2) While on flying or training duty away from their Permanent Domicile.

  b. If the Company does not provide hotel accommodations, the Captain shall:
  1) Obtain suitable lodging for the crew; and
  2) Claim reasonable actual lodging expense on their expense account form supported by hotel
  receipts.

  c. The Company shall provide an International Pilot voluntarily awarded a Flight Grouping
  originating at other than their Domicile with hotel accommodations (at Company expense) in any
  Domicile (except their own) to accomplish the pilot’s flight duties.

  2. Hotels must have the following required items to be considered suitable pilot hotels on an initial and
  on-going basis:
  a. Safety:
  1) Sprinklers
  2) Smoke Detector
  3) Emergency lighting
  4) Effective and safe egress paths and stairwells
  5) Guestroom phone should have outside-line accessibility
  6) Staff emergency training
  7) Electronic key
  8) Secondary door lock
  9) Alarm system

  b. Security
  1) Rooms assigned above ground level
  2) No exterior corridors
  3) Windows/Sliders w/secondary lock

  c. Quiet
  1) Should be able to get adequate rest

  d. Guestroom
  1) Single occupancy
  2) Expedited check-in
  3) No credit card required
  4) Non-smoking
  5) Pilot rooms shall be assigned to the highest available floor (non-upgrade)
  6) Black out curtains
  7) Complimentary In-Room WIFI internet

  trousers, one (1) tie, and two (2) shirts every twelve (12) months, or sooner at Company discretion,
  based upon reasonable wear.

  required) every thirty-six (36) months, or sooner at Company discretion, based upon reasonable
  wear.

  recommendations of the Master Executive Council.

  1. The Company shall make every reasonable effort to provide or arrange free parking for pilots at their
  Domiciles. Should free parking space not be available, the Company will pay the pilot, upon
  presentation of a receipt, any excess over five dollars ($5.00) that the employee has to pay monthly.
  If the employee requests, they may pay through payroll deduction.

  2. If a pilot does not claim parking expense at their Domicile, such pilot may claim parking expense at
  one other location and the Company shall reimburse such pilot the excess over five ($5.00) dollars
  that such pilot has to pay monthly to a maximum of what such pilot’s parking expense would have
  been had they parked at their Domicile. In addition to any other reimbursable parking expense, a
  pilot assigned a flight or reserve duty at a Domicile other than their own may claim monthly parking
  expense at the assigned Domicile.

  award or assignment. No space available ticket will be issued when the pre-booked load factor is

  unlikely, the pilot may upgrade their ticket to positive space and be reimbursed therefore.

  reasonable actual expenses of each pilot transferring from one Domicile to another Domicile, for
  hotel and meals, to the extent such expenses are supported by receipts.

A. PILOT TRANSFERRED TO AN ADMINISTRATIVE PILOT ROLE

  1. An Administrative Pilot is any pilot who has been transferred to an administrative role for the
  Company.

  a. Such pilot shall retain and continue to accrue seniority on the Pilots’ System Seniority List
  provided such pilot maintains at all times the pilot’s medical certificate required by their
  status.

  2. If such pilot permits their pilot’s medical certificate to lapse, they shall retain the Seniority
  already accrued to the time of such lapse, and shall have a period not to exceed one (1) year in
  which to regain their pilot’s medical certificate. If they regain such pilot’s medical certificate
  within one (1) year, their Seniority shall commence to accrue from the date their medical
  certificate is so regained.

B. PERMANENT BID PROCEDURE FOR ADMINISTRATIVE PILOTS

  1. Administrative Pilots who are on the Pilots’ System Seniority List will retain the permanent
  Category Vacancy and Domicile held at the time of transfer to such position for reinstatement to
  line flying unless awarded or assigned another Category Vacancy and Domicile pursuant to
  Subparagraphs 8.B.3 and 8.B.4.

  2. An Administrative Pilot will be required to maintain and participate in the Standing Bid process
  in the same manner as an active line pilot.

  3. An Administrative Pilot who is awarded a change in their Permanent Category Vacancy and
  Domicile will have that bid award recorded as a change for reinstatement to line flying purposes
  only.

  4. An Administrative Pilot returning to line flying will be reinstated to the last Permanent Category
  Vacancy and Domicile they are holding at the time of return. If a pilot is not currently qualified
  in the Permanent Category Vacancy they are holding at the time of reinstatement, such pilot may
  be required to fly in any equipment in which they are currently qualified until training and
  qualification for the Permanent Category Vacancy they hold at the time of reinstatement can be
  accomplished pursuant to Section 9 (Training). Provided the pilot is not in training, they shall be
  guaranteed the same number of total scheduled days off as is contained in the line of flying to
  which their Seniority would have entitled them had they been so qualified. The pilot shall have
  the option of taking all such days off at the pilot’s currently awarded Domicile or the pilot’s
  former Domicile. If training has not begun within ninety (90) days after reinstatement, then such
  pilot shall be entitled to Bypass Pay as specified in Subsection 20.M (Bypass).

  1. Administrative Pilots who are on the Pilots’ System Seniority List may each fly a total of three
  hundred sixty (360) Pay and Credit hours (aggregate total of all categories) per calendar year

  Credit hours in any calendar month.

  intention to remove the fleet type and:

  period.

  an eligible fleet and, in the case of an Evaluator Pilot have been so for a minimum of one (1) year.

A. FEDERAL AVIATION REGULATION LIMITS.

  1. If a pilot awarded/assigned a Bid Run or Flight Grouping that would cause such pilot to be in violation of any
  flight time, flight duty period, or rest limitation as defined by the Federal Aviation Regulations, then the
  Company will relieve such pilot from enough flight time or duty necessary to comply with such Federal
  Aviation Regulation and Pay and Credit the pilot the scheduled time for all such Segment(s).

B. TIME USED TO DETERMINE MAXIMUM PAY AND CREDIT TIME

  1. All Pay and Credit time shall be used to determine the maximum Pay and Credit limitations for the
  purposes of monthly bidding. The following shall be included to determine the maximum pilot
  Pay and Credit limits for the purposes of monthly bidding :
  a. The scheduled or actual time block-to-block (Subparagraph 4.B.1);
  b. Minimum Daily Guarantee (Subparagraph 4.C.1 or 4.C.3);
  c. MFGC (Subparagraph 4.C.1 or 4.C.3)
  d. Duty Rig (Subparagraph 4.C.1);
  e. Trip Rig (Subparagraph 4.C.1 or 4.C.3);
  f. ALPA Flight Pay Loss (Subsection 4.G);
  g. Segment Pay (Subsection 4.M).
  h. Vacation Pay (Subsection 6.J);
  i. Deadhead Pay (Subsection 7.B);
  j. Training Pay (Section 9);
  k. Sick Leave Pay (Subsection 12.B);
  l. All credited flight time and all other Pay and Credit as provided for elsewhere in this Agreement.

C. FAR TIME LIMITS

  1. The flight time limitations and required rest periods for pilots set forth in Federal Air Regulations
  in force and effect on the date this Agreement is signed shall continue in effect for the Company’s
  operations.

  2. In the event that such flight time limitations and required rest periods for pilots, as set forth in the
  Federal Air Regulations, are altered or amended by the appropriate government agency,
  conferences may be initiated either by the President of the Company or the President of the
  Association for the purpose of determining whether such alterations or amendments shall apply to
  the Company’s operations.

  3. Prior to submitting a Fatigue Risk Management system (FRMS) application or an exemption to
  FAR 117 to the FAA for approval, the Company will obtain ALPA's consent. Such consent
  with not be unreasonably withheld and, if withheld, will be based solely on the merits of the
  FRMS or exemption application.
  a. Disagreements regarding any matter in Section 10.C.3 above must be resolved, including, if
  necessary, through an expedited grievance/arbitration process, before the Company may
  submit an FRMS application to the FAA. Both parties will abide by the arbitration decision.

  duty, except that in no case shall leave for sickness or injury exceed a total continuous period

C. DRUG AND ALCOHOL TESTING

  1. A pilot will not be required to submit to a drug or alcohol test on a day free of duty. In the event a
  drug or alcohol test interferes with a pilot’s schedule, the pilot shall not suffer any loss of pay or
  credit as a result of such drug or alcohol test. A pilot who is required to submit to a drug or alcohol
  test upon release from a Duty Period, shall receive one (1) hour pay/no credit for such drug or
  alcohol test. Time spent submitting to a drug or alcohol test shall not be considered duty for the
  purposes of the Agreement if such test is taken after the completion of all of that pilot’s flights for
  that day.

  2. At the time a drug test is administered, a “split sample” will be taken. The cost of maintaining the
  “chain of custody” and the test itself will be borne by the Company. One of the samples will be used
  for the drug test. The second sample will be retained and stored in a manner which will preserve its
  validity as a test sample, and which comports with “chain of custody” requirements. In the event the
  first sample tests negative, the stored sample will be destroyed. In the event the first sample tests
  positive, the stored sample shall be tested at a facility used by the Company which is different from
  the facility used to test the first sample or, at the pilot’s option, at a prearranged DHHS/NIDA-
  approved facility designated by ALPA. In the event the stored sample tests negative, it shall void the
  results of the first sample. Costs associated with the “chain of custody” and the testing of the stored
  sample shall be borne by the Company, provided a Company-selected facility is used, or, if the pilot
  selects another facility, the Company shall pay an amount equal to the cost of maintaining the “chain
  of custody” and the testing at the Company-selected facility.

  a. At the completion of an alcohol confirmation test, any pilot who has an alcohol test result of 0.02

  a. A pilot who is in treatment and/or rehabilitation will be allowed, but not required, to use all of

SECTION 14 WORKERS’ COMPENSATION & OCCUPATIONAL INJURY BENEFITS

A. WORKERS’ COMPENSATION BENEFITS

  1. Workers’ compensation benefits shall be provided by the Company for all pilots and shall be in
  amounts equal to those prescribed by the Workers’ Compensation Law of the State of Hawaii, or the
  State of pilot’s Domicile, whichever provides the greater benefit to the pilot.

B. MONETARY BENEFITS

  1. The monetary benefits so paid shall be in addition to any monetary benefits paid pursuant to the
  provisions of Subsection 15.A (Qualification of Compensation Benefits) and shall be paid to the
  beneficiaries prescribed by the applicable law as herein provided.

C. OCCUPATIONAL INJURY

  1. Occupational injury as used in this Section means any illness or injury that is covered by workers’
  compensation insurance under applicable State Laws.

D. OCCUPATIONAL INJURY PAYMENT

  1. Any pilot who suffers an occupational injury shall follow the applicable State Workers’
  Compensation laws for timely reporting of their occupational injury. Occupational injury pay will
  commence once the claim has been deemed compensable according to the applicable State Workers’
  Compensation laws. Occupational injury pay shall be equivalent to the pilot’s current earnings, or an
  average of their previous twelve (12) months earnings, exclusive of leaves, whichever is greater, less
  taxes and workers’ compensation, for a period up to and including three (3) months. If an
  occupational injury continues beyond such three (3) month period, occupational injury pay
  equivalent to two-thirds (2/3) of the pilot’s earnings stipulated above, less taxes and workers’
  compensation, shall be paid for up to and including nine (9) additional months.

E. CHARGING OCCUPATIONAL INJURY

  1. Such occupational injury benefits shall in no way be charged against a pilot’s non-occupational sick
  leave provided for in Section 12 (Sick Leave). Once a pilot’s occupational injury claim has been
  deemed compensable according to the applicable State Workers’ Compensation laws, the Company
  shall restore any and all sick leave the pilot used because of the occupational injury between the date
  of the workplace injury and the date the workplace injury is deemed compensable. If a pilot had no,
  or insufficient, sick leave available to use between the date of the workplace injury and the date the
  workplace injury is deemed compensable, the Company shall compensate the pilot for any income
  lost during this time period, as defined in 14.D.1.

F. MODIFIED DUTIES

  1. In the event that a pilot receiving Workers’ Compensation or OCC benefits is released by his
  physician to perform light or modified duties, the Company may assign such pilot to perform such
  duties in accordance with Company policy in effect as of the effective date of this Agreement, to the
  extent that such assignment is required under applicable Workers’ Compensation law.

  reasonably have knowledge upon which the grievance is based. This does not preclude claims for
  adjustment arising out of bookkeeping errors beyond ninety (90) days.

  contact the Chief Pilot or his designee. The pilot shall specifically indicate that he is contacting the
  Chief Pilot for the purpose of arranging a consultation under this provision of the Agreement.

  a. The Chief Pilot shall consult with the pilot with regard to their dispute or potential grievance and
  they shall make every effort to resolve the dispute without the need for a grievance.

  b. The Chief Pilot shall have the necessary authority to resolve the ordinary disputes likely to arise
  from time to time.

  c. In the case of disputes that would otherwise be filed as group grievances or MEC grievances, the

  Subparagraphs 16.A.2.a and 16.A.2.c should be made by the pilot as soon as possible after the
  incident giving rise to the dispute or potential grievance and, in any case, must be made within
  the ninety (90) day time limit provided by Subparagraph 16.A.1, and that time limit shall not be
  extended by operation of this provision unless mutually agreed.

  3. In the event the dispute is not resolved in accordance with Subparagraph 16.A.2, a grievance,

C. PERMANENT GRIEVANCE MEDIATION PROGRAM

  1. Grievance mediation sessions will be scheduled at earliest available date whenever at least ten (10)

  mediator is available

  2. In the case of a grievance filed by an individual Pilot, the grievant will elect to attend the Mediation
  Conference in person or by telephone conference, or he will arrange to be represented by an
  authorized Association representative. The grievant will authorize such representative to act on his
  behalf. If a pilot chooses to be present it will not be at Company expense.

  3. In the case of consolidated grievances, group grievances, or grievances filed by an Association
  Representative, the designated Association Representative present shall represent the Association
  and all Pilot parties to such grievances.

  4. Both parties acknowledge the importance of having participants at the Mediation Conference who
  have complete authority to resolve the grievances. In addition, every effort will be made to insure
  that there are Association and Company Representatives present at each Mediation Conference who
  are knowledgeable of the subject matter pertaining to the grievances to be considered at the
  Conference.

  5. The Company and the Association shall each appoint a principal spokesperson for each mediated
  case.

  6. Proceedings before the mediator will be informal in nature and the rules of evidence will not apply.
  The presentation of evidence, documentation, arguments, etc., will not be limited to that which was
  presented at the prior stages of the grievance procedure.

  7. The parties will promptly write a settlement agreement to document grievance settlements reached
  during the Mediation Conference. The parties shall mutually agree as to whether the settlement will
  constitute precedent, and this understanding will be included in the written settlement document.

  8. Other than a settlement document resulting from a successful mediation, no record in any form or
  medium of the Mediation Conference will be made. Any material that is presented to the mediator
  will be returned to the party presenting that material at the termination of the Mediation Conference,
  and no copy will be retained by the Mediator or any other person or party.

  9. The mediator will have the authority to meet separately with either the Association or the Company
  in the Mediation Conference, but will not have the authority to compel the resolution of the
  grievance.

  10. If no settlement is reached during the Mediation Conference, and only at the joint request of both
  parties, the mediator may provide an immediate oral advisory decision. When rendering an oral
  advisory decision, the mediator will state the grounds for such decision. Unless accepted by both
  parties, this decision will not be binding.

A. ESTABLISHMENT OF SYSTEM BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT

  1. In compliance with Section 204, Title II of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, there is hereby
  established a System Board of Adjustment, which shall be known as the “Hawaiian Airlines Pilots
  System Board of Adjustment,” hereinafter referred to as the “Board.” The Board’s purpose shall be
  to adjust and decide disputes that may arise under the terms of the Pilots’ Agreement when such
  disputes have been properly submitted to the Board.

B. COMPOSITION OF THE BOARD

  1. The Board shall consist of three (3) members or four (4) members as provided below:

  2. The four (4) member Board shall consist of two (2) members selected and appointed by the
  Association, and two (2) members selected and appointed by the Company, and such appointees
  shall be known as “Board Members.” In addition, the Association and Company shall each
  designate an alternate and, in the event of the unavailability of a Board Member, the respective
  alternate shall act as a Board Member in place of the absent Board Member. In the event one or the
  other party wishes to conduct a Board Meeting with only one of that party’s Board Members present,
  that Board Member shall cast two (2) votes on matters before the Board.

  3. The three (3) member Board shall consist of one (1) member selected and appointed by the
  Association, and one member selected and appointed by the Company, and such appointees shall be
  known as “Board Members.” In addition, the Association and the Company shall each designate an
  alternate, and, in the event of the unavailability of a Board Member, the respective alternate shall act
  as a Board Member in place of the absent Board Member. The third member of the Board shall be
  the Referee (also known as the “Arbitrator”), who shall be selected as provided in Subsection 17.E
  (Panel of Referees (Arbitrators)).

  4. Board Members appointed by the Company, and Board Members appointed by the Association, and
  their alternates, shall serve for one (1) year from the date of their appointment and, thereafter, until
  their successors have been duly appointed. Vacancies shall be filled in the same manner as is
  provided herein for the selection and appointment of the original Board Members and the original
  alternates.

  5. The Company will ensure that grievances heard on appeal by management personnel will not be
  heard by the same person rendering a decision at an earlier step of the process. It is intended that
  these steps will provide for an unbiased and objective review of the circumstances and applicable
  contract provisions in each grievance.

  6. The Board Members shall select a Chairperson and a Vice Chairperson, both of whom shall be
  members of the Board. The term of office of Chairperson and Vice Chairperson shall be one (1)
  year. Thereafter, from year to year, the Board shall designate one (1) of its members to act as
  Chairperson and one (1) to act as Vice Chairperson for one (1) year terms.

  7. The office of Chairperson shall be filled and held alternately by a Board Member appointed by the
  Association and by a Board Member appointed by the Company. When a Board Member appointed
  by the Association is Chairperson, a Board Member appointed by the Company shall be Vice
  Chairperson, and vice versa. Both shall have a vote in connection with all actions taken by the
  Board. The Referee shall preside at meetings and hearings of the three (3) member Board.

  changes in hours of employment, rates of compensation, or working conditions covered by existing

  2. The Board shall consider any dispute properly submitted to it by the President of the Association or
  by the Company, when such dispute has not been previously settled in accordance with the terms
  provided for in Section 16 (Grievances).

D. PROCEEDINGS BEFORE THE BOARD

  1. All disputes properly submitted to the Board for consideration shall be addressed to the Members of
  the Board, including all papers and exhibits in connection therewith. Each case submitted shall show:

  a.  Question or questions at issue;
  b.  Statement of facts;
  c.  Position of employee or employees; and
  d.  Position of the Company.

  2. When possible, joint submissions should be made, but if the parties are unable to agree upon a joint
  submission, then either party may submit the dispute and its position to the Board. No matter shall
  be considered by the Board that has not first been handled in accordance with the provisions of
  Section 16 (Grievances) and a decision thereon by the Company.

  3. Upon receipt of notice of the submission of a dispute, the Chairman shall set a date for hearing,
  which shall be at the time of the next regular meeting of the Board, as provided in Subparagraph
  17.B.7, or, if at least one (1) Board Member considers the matter of sufficient urgency and
  importance, then at such earlier date and at such place as the Chairperson and Vice Chairperson shall
  agree upon, but not more than fifteen (15) days after such request for meeting is made by at least one
  (1) of said Board Members, and the Chairperson shall give the necessary notices in writing of such
  meeting to the Board Members, the Referee, and to the parties to the dispute.

  4. Employees covered by this Agreement may be represented at Board hearings by such person or
  persons as they may choose and designate, and the Company may be represented by such person or
  persons as it may choose and designate. Evidence may be presented either orally, or in writing, or
  both.

  5. On request of any individual Board Member, the Board shall summon any witnesses who are
  employed by the Company and who may be deemed necessary by the parties to the dispute, or by

  case is otherwise finally resolved.

  4. The parties may fill vacancies on the panel at any time by mutual agreement and will agree upon and
  attempt to maintain a list of four (4) alternates for this purpose. When a vacancy on the panel occurs,
  it will be filled by randomly selecting a name from the list of alternates. In the event there are no

  Notwithstanding any provision of Section 16 (Grievances), or Section 17 (System Board), or any other
  provision of the current Pilots’ Agreement to the contrary, the following rules and procedures for the
  disposition of grievances submitted for mediation/arbitration shall apply:

  1. Composition of the Board. The Board shall consist of a single member who shall serve as
  “Mediator/Arbitrator” during the special meeting of the Board. The Mediator/Arbitrator shall be
  appointed by agreement of the Parties. In the event a Mediator/Arbitrator shall become unable or
  unwilling to complete his service on the Board, the Parties will meet promptly and agree to a
  replacement Mediator/Arbitrator.

  2. Agenda. The Company and the Association shall promptly meet and agree upon an agenda for the
  meeting, which shall list all pending grievances and disputes that the Parties agree to submit to
  mediation/arbitration in the order that the disputes will be considered. Disputes involving the same or
  similar issues, or the same subject area or the same grievant may be grouped to be mediated at the
  same time.

  The final agenda will be set not less than two weeks prior to the commencement of mediation. A
  copy of the agenda with a brief description of the matters at issue in each case will be provided to the
  Mediator/Arbitrator.

  3. Meeting Schedule. The Mediator/Arbitrator, in consultation with the Parties, shall schedule an initial
  one (1) week session during which all grievances and disputes placed on the agenda by the Parties
  shall be submitted to mediation by the Mediator/Arbitrator. If all grievances on the agenda cannot be
  mediated during that session, the Mediator/Arbitrator shall schedule an additional session or sessions
  as required to complete the agenda.

  4. Procedures for Individual Grievances. Pilots who have individual grievances, shall be notified of the
  approximate date and, if possible, time set for their grievances to be mediated and that the
  Association will represent the grievant unless they wish to select one of three (3) other options: (1)
  they may appear in person or by phone conference and represent themself, or (2) they may appoint a
  Hawaiian pilot of their choice to represent them , provided the pilot agrees, or (3) they may
  permanently withdraw his grievance. In the event the grievant is represented by the Association, the
  grievant will be permitted to attend the mediation/arbitration session along with the Association
  representative should they wish to do so. The grievant will also be notified that any and all evidence,
  documentation, statements, arguments, etc., that they wish to be considered during mediation and, if
  necessary, for arbitration, must be submitted to the Board no later than the mediation session for the
  grievance. Similarly, any evidence, documentation, statements, arguments, etc., that the Company
  wishes to be considered must be submitted at that time.

  5. Procedures for Group and MEC/LEC Grievances. The Company and the Association will each be
  represented by such person or persons as they may select. Each will also provide such evidence,
  documentation, statements, arguments, etc., as they may wish to be considered.

  6. Rules During Mediation and Arbitration. Mediation sessions shall be conducted on an informal
  basis. Formal rules of evidence shall not apply except that the Mediator/Arbitrator may apply such
  rules of evidence as they shall deem necessary and proper to his consideration of any cases which
  must be resolved by them acting as Arbitrator.

  7. Mediation Settlements. Any settlement made as the result of mediation shall be by voluntary mutual
  agreement of the grievant or the Association, as the case may be, and the Company. Grievants who
  appoint representatives or request representation by the Association shall grant such representative

A. SENIORITY GENERAL

  1. Seniority as a pilot shall be based upon the length of service as a pilot with the Company.

  2. Seniority shall begin to accrue from the date a pilot is first employed by the Company as an airline
  pilot and shall continue to accrue during such period of employment. Pilots hired on the same day
  shall be placed on the Seniority List in accordance with the last four digits of their social security
  number, the employee having the lowest number given the higher position on the Seniority List.

  3. Seniority shall govern all pilots in case of promotion and demotion, their retention in case of
  reduction in force or reduction in schedules, their re-employment after release due to reduction in
  force, their selection of vacancies and runs, and all other rights, privileges, and opportunities
  accorded to pilots under this Agreement.

B. SENIORITY DATE

  1. Any pilot, once having established a Seniority date hereunder, shall not lose that date except as
  provided in this Agreement.

  2. When a junior pilot is promoted over a senior pilot, by reason of the failure of the latter to qualify in
  their turn, the senior pilot shall continue to retain their position on the Pilots System Seniority List.

C. PILOTS’ SYSTEM SENIORITY LIST

  1. The Company shall post on its website a list of names of all pilots, arranged in the order of system
  Seniority. Such list shall be known as the Pilot System Seniority List and shall contain the names of
  all pilots entitled to Seniority, whether active or inactive, and the date of employment of each pilot
  indicating the Seniority to which the pilot is entitled. Such list shall thereafter be brought up to date
  as of January 1 and July 1 of each year and posted within thirty (30) days thereafter. Any changes
  from the preceding list shall be prominently noted.

  2. A grievance based upon an error or omission of the Pilots’ System Seniority List must be filed within
  thirty (30) days after the first posting on which such an error or omission is reflected, except that a
  pilot on vacation, furlough, or leave of absence may exercise this right within thirty (30) days
  following their return to active duty.

D. PROMOTION

  1. The Company may give pilots an opportunity to qualify in any higher category at any time.
  Promotions to a higher category shall be in the order of seniority, subject to this Section, provided
  that pilots who have been given the opportunity to qualify in a higher category, and are unable to do
  so, shall not hold up the promotion of other pilots junior to them. Such cases shall be handled in
  accordance with Subparagraph 18.B.2.

A. NOTICE OF FURLOUGH

  1. A pilot shall receive not less than fourteen (14) calendar days advance notice in writing of any
  furlough, or shall be paid two (2) weeks pay in lieu thereof; except that a pilot who has completed
  their probationary period shall:

  c. They shall not be issued more than one (1) furlough notice in any calendar month;

  d. The pay provision shall not apply when conditions outside the Company’s control render such
  notice impossible; such conditions as:
  1) War or foreign invasion;
  2) Strikes;
  3) Mandatory grounding of aircraft;
  4) Official state of emergency; or
  5) Act of God.

  2. Prior to the posting of a Permanent Vacancy and/or Displacement Bulletin that reduces the total
  number of Permanent Vacancies, the Company shall offer a leave of absence to pilots in the category
  where the excess exists.

  a. A pilot shall update their Standing Bid. That update shall include their:

  Permanent Vacancies in order of Seniority to recalled pilots.

B. CLASSIFICATION OF VACANCIES

  1. All Category Vacancies shall be classified as either Permanent Vacancies or temporary Vacancies.

  2. Permanent Vacancy: A Permanent Vacancy shall be any Vacancy which is anticipated to exist, or
  actually exists, for ninety (90) days or more at an existing or new permanent Domicile. Permanent
  Vacancies shall be either primary or secondary. A primary vacancy is one that is created as a result
  of initial (new) or added flying time in a category(-ies) at a Domicile, by acquisition of new
  equipment, retirement (early, disability or normal), death, resignation, a pilot’s failure to qualify for
  an awarded Vacancy, sustained termination, or when the Company desires to increase staffing at any
  Domicile. A secondary vacancy is the Category Vacancy created by the holder of a Permanent
  Vacancy when they leaves to fill another Permanent Vacancy. All active pilots, supervisory pilots,
  and pilots on a leave of absence shall hold a Permanent Category Vacancy at a permanent Domicile.

  3. Temporary Vacancy: Temporary Vacancies shall be classified as follows:

  a. Type I - Temporary Upgrade Vacancy (1-62 days): A Type I Temporary Upgrade Vacancy is a
  vacancy that is anticipated to exist for sixty-two (62) or fewer days and is used to allow a pilot to
  temporarily upgrade to a higher Category than such pilot’s permanent category (as specified in
  Subparagraph 20.A.3) in such pilot’s permanently awarded equipment and Domicile. Type I
  Temporaries shall be posted within both the equipment and Domicile to which the vacancy(-ies)
  apply and will be available for bid by all pilots in that equipment and Domicile who are currently
  qualified to fill such Vacancy(-ies) and who are presently flying in a Category lower than the
  temporary Category posted for bid (see Subparagraph 20.D.2).

  b. Type II - Temporary Category Vacancy (1-62 days): A Type II Temporary Category Vacancy is
  a Vacancy that is anticipated to exist for sixty-two (62) or fewer days and is used to allow a pilot
  to temporarily perform flight duty in a different category than such pilot’s Permanent Category
  Vacancy (as specified in Subparagraph 20.A.1) within such pilot’s permanent Domicile. Type II
  Temporaries shall be posted within the equipment and Domicile to which the Vacancy(-ies)
  apply and will be available for bid by all pilots in that Domicile who are currently qualified to fill
  such Vacancy(-ies) (see Subparagraphs 20.D.2 and 20.E.6).

c. Type III - Temporary Duty Vacancy (1-62) days: A Type III Temporary Duty Vacancy is a

  allow a pilot to perform flight duty in such pilot’s permanent category Vacancy at a Domicile

  Vacancy(-ies) shall be posted for System-Wide Bid pursuant to the provisions of this Section 20

  posted for system-wide bid on the first weekday following the ninety-second (92nd) day after
  Activation pursuant to the provisions of this Section 20 (Filling of Vacancies).

  c. Extension: Any Temporary Vacancy awarded or assigned pursuant to this Section 20 (Filling of
  Vacancies) may be extended, at Company option, for a period not to exceed an additional thirty-
  one (31) days due to unforeseen circumstances beyond the Company’s control, and which were
  not a preplanned part of the vacancy. An extension of a pilot’s vacancy will not alter the
  temporary classification of that vacancy, and the pilot filling such vacancy shall continue to
  receive expense allowances and Pay and Credit under the original terms of the award or
  assignment. An extension of a Type I, Type II, or Type III Temporary Vacancy shall not waive

M. ELECTION NOT TO TRAIN

  1. The Company may choose not to award a new Category Vacancy to any pilot who, at the time of the
  Effective Date of the Vacancy Award, will be within twenty-four (24) months of the FAA mandatory
  retirement age.

  a. The above provision shall not apply to a pilot who is awarded a different Category Vacancy in
  the same aircraft type (e.g., upgrading from a First Officer to a Captain), and

  b. Shall not apply to Displacement Procedures (PWA Subsection 20.I).

  c. Exception: The Company may not bypass a pilot within twenty-four (24) months of the date they
  reach the regulatory age limit for pilots unless the Company has bypassed all pilots holding a
  Category Vacancy Award to the same Category with:
  1) the same Effective Date,
  2) the same training requirements, and
  3) earlier mandatory retirement dates.

  1. A System Awards and Assignment Committee shall be established for the purpose of implementing
  the procedures relating to the filling of Vacancies as set forth in this Section 20 (Filling of

  following:

  a. Promulgating and maintaining a clear, concise, and complete written statement of the rules,
  practices, and procedures governing the creation of Vacancies at Domiciles for bidding upon and
  awarding of assignment to such Vacancies and termination of existing or prospective Vacancies.

  b. Preparation of recommendations relative to the opening or closing of pilot Domiciles or the
  addition of or discontinuance of Category(-ies) of flying at an existing Domicile.

  c. Monitoring the award or assignment of all Category vacancies system-wide. Pilot members
  shall be notified of the date, time, and place of such awards and may be present at the award or
  assignment of each Vacancy.

  d. Reviewing disputes that arise out of the administration of this Section and preparing
  recommendations as to the disposition of such disputes.

  e. Ensuring that the displacement and bypass procedures set forth in Subsections 20.I
  (Displacement Procedures) and 20.L (Bypass), respectively, are correctly administered.

  2. Composition of Committee

  a. The system Awards and Assignment Committee shall be composed of not more than four (4)
  members, two (2) of whom shall be selected by the Company and two (2) of whom shall be
  selected by the pilots’ MEC. The Company and the pilots may each select two (2) alternate
  members who may act for their respective primaries. Each party shall notify the other in writing
  of the selection of members and alternates, each of who shall continue to serve until replaced
  pursuant to further written notification.

  b. Committee Chairman. The Company shall designate one (1) of its appointees as Chairman of
  the committee and shall keep all committee members currently informed of such appointment.

  committee records and correspondence, and implementing committee actions. They shall carry
  out these duties in a manner fair and impartial to all interested parties, and shall consult with, and
  give full credence to, all committee members on any issues, however, the Chairman shall have
  full voting rights. Committee records shall be readily accessible to all committee members.

  committee members. Fifty per cent (50%) of the committee members may call a meeting upon

A. AWARDING OF RUNS

  1. Each month, the holders of Category Vacancies at each Domicile shall be awarded a Monthly Run.
  The Flight Groupings for such runs shall be prepared, posted for bid, and awarded in accordance
  with the principles set forth in this Section 21 (Preparation, Bidding, and Awarding of Runs).

B. PREPARATION OF FLIGHT GROUPINGS FOR MONTHLY RUNS

  1. Crew Planning will obtain monthly flight time projections from Network Planning and assure that:

  a. The Flight Groupings have been prepared in such a way as to minimize the need for changing
  pilot schedules; and

  b. A sufficient number of Category Vacancies are awarded (pursuant to the provisions of Section
  20 (Filling of Vacancies)) in order to accommodate projected flying and provide an adequate
  Reserve.

  2. It shall be the responsibility of Network Planning when contemplating a change in daily schedules to
  provide Crew Planning with information necessary to prepare the Flight Groupings for pilots’
  selection at least thirty (30) days prior to the effective day of such schedule change in order to meet
  the posting limitation provided in Subsection 21.D (Notification of Bidding Period for Monthly
  Runs).

  3. One hundred percent (100%) of the known flying at each Domicile shall be used to construct the
  Flight Groupings for the pilots to preference on their Monthly Runs.

  4. The criteria for preparation of monthly Flight Groupings are:

  a. Flight Groupings will, where possible, be constructed so as to provide not less than forty-five
  (45) minutes between Round Trips for international flights and not less than twenty (20) minutes
  between Round Trips for interisland flights.

  b. Flight Groupings shall be constructed so as to comply with Section 10 (Hours of Service).

  c. Flight Groupings will usually contain maximum scheduled block hours for minimum Duty
  Period hours, consistent with the above criteria.

  5. The following information shall be included on all Monthly Run Flight Groupings:

  a.  Flight numbers
  b.  Date and day of departure and arrival
  c.  Time of departure and arrival (GMT and Local Domicile Time)
  d.  Published block pay time for each segment
  e.  Beginning and end time of each Duty Period
  f.  Layover times (RON)
  g.  Total duty hours away from Domicile (including preflight and post-flight requirements).
  h.  A designation if it is to be operated with an augmented crew.

  6. The Flight Groupings shall not be altered or changed between the time and date of posting of the
  Bidding Period and the date of the awarding of Monthly Runs.

  1. Once the Bid Award process is complete, the Minimum Reserve Number (MRN) for each
  calendar day will be determined for the month. The MRN shall be calculated as follows:

  a. The net reserve number for a given calendar day is the number of awarded Reserve pilots for
  that day, minus the number of uncovered Flight Groupings in open time operating that day.

  b. The MRN is the net reserve number for that day, reduced by one for every fifty (50) eligible
  bid pilots in that Category, rounded up to the next multiple of fifty (50).

A. SCHEDULING POLICY

  1. The purpose of the scheduling policy is to promulgate a clear, concise, and complete written
  statement of the rules, practices, and procedures relative to the scheduling of pilots, and to ensure
  that all provisions of the Agreement shall be fairly and equitably implemented and uniformly applied
  to all pilots.

  2. The success of the airline depends upon it providing good service by means of an efficient and
  economical operation. Its pilots are entitled to the best working conditions this Agreement and the
  Scheduling Policy can provide.

  3. Where any rule or provision is not clear, its interpretation and application shall be consistent with the
  following three (3) principles:

  a. Neither party shall adopt strained or unreasonable interpretations to evade a duty or an
  obligation, or to accomplish a purpose that could not otherwise be accomplished.

  b. Company representatives should recognize that economy and expediency themselves do not
  justify a departure from applicable rules.

  c. Except as otherwise provided in this Agreement, a pilot’s schedule shall not be changed
  (including recall or the cancellation of a scheduled day off) when the exercise of reasonable
  resourcefulness and diligence could or would have prevented such change.

  4. The Chief Pilot is responsible for the scheduling of pilots pursuant to the provisions of the PWA.

  5. Individual pilots are responsible for obtaining their schedules from Crew Scheduling as set forth in
  this Section.

B. SCHEDULING PROTESTS

  1. When a pilot questions the legality of a flight schedule assigned them by Crew Scheduling, they shall
  so notify the Scheduling Clerk, after which the following procedure shall be implemented:

  a. The Scheduling Clerk receiving the verbal protest will immediately review the protested flight
  schedule with the Director–Crew Scheduling (or designee) in an attempt to resolve the issue.

  b. In the absence of the Director–Crew Scheduling (or designee), the Scheduling Clerk will contact
  one of the following management officials in the order listed:
  1) Chief Pilot, or
  2) Director–Flight Operations; or
  3) Vice-President of Flight Operations

  c. If it is determined that such protested flight schedule is:
  1) Legal, the pilot will accept and comply with the protested flight schedule unless relieved
  therefrom by Crew Scheduling.
  2) Illegal, the management official contacted shall promptly relieve the pilot from the protested
  flight schedule.

  d. If the pilot is not relieved from the protested assignment and still feels the assignment is illegal,
  they should file a Scheduling Clarification Request (SCR).

  the number of flight assignments to reserve pilots that day, as the remaining reserve pilot
  would have only four days of availability to cover the remaining five-day Flight Grouping. In
  this case, the “Fly Me” preference would not be honored, so the four-day-availability LCR

A. COLLECTIVE BARGAINING SERVICE CHARGE

  1. Each employee of the Company covered by this Agreement who fails to voluntarily acquire or
  maintain membership in the Association shall be required, as a condition of continued
  employment, beginning thirty (30) days after the effective date of this Agreement or thirty (30)
  days after the completion of their probationary period, whichever is later, to pay to the
  Association each month a service charge as a contribution for the administration of this
  Agreement and the representation of such employee. The service charge for the first month shall
  be in an amount equal to the Association’s regular and usual monthly dues, and for each month
  thereafter.

  2. If any employee of the Company covered by this Agreement becomes delinquent in the payment
  of their service charges or membership dues, the Association shall notify such employee by
  registered mail, return receipt requested, copy to the Vice President-Flight Operations of the
  Company, that they is delinquent in the payment of such service charge or membership dues as
  specified herein and is subject to discharge as an employee of the Company. Such letter shall
  also notify the employee that they must remit the required payment within a period of fifteen (15)
  days or be discharged.

  3. If, upon the expiration of the fifteen (15) day period, the employee still remains delinquent, the
  Association shall certify in writing to the Vice President-Flight Operations, copy to the employee,
  that the employee has failed to remit payment within the grace period allowed and is therefore to
  be discharged. The Vice President-Flight Operations shall thereupon take proper steps to
  discharge such employee from the service of the Company.

  4. A grievance by an employee who is to be discharged as a result of an interpretation or application
  of the provisions of Section 23 (Union Security) shall be subject to the following procedures:

  a. An employee who believes that the provisions of Section 23 (Union Security) have not been
  properly interpreted or applied as it pertains to them may submit their request for review in
  writing within five (5) days from the date of their notification by the Vice President-Flight
  Operations, as provided in Subparagraph 23.A.3. The request must be submitted to the Vice
  President-Flight Operations, or their designee, who will review the grievance and render their
  decision in writing not later than five (5) days following receipt of the grievance.

  b. The Vice President-Flight Operations, or designee, shall forward their decision to the
  employee, with a copy to the Association. Said decision shall be final and binding on all
  interested parties unless appealed as hereinafter provided. If the decision is not satisfactory to
  either the employee or the Association, then either may appeal the grievance within ten (10)
  days from the date of the decision directly to a neutral Referee who may be agreed upon by
  the Company and the Association within ten (10) days thereafter. In the event the parties fail
  to agree upon a neutral Referee within the specified period, either the Company or the
  Association may request the National Mediation Board to name such neutral Referee. The
  decision of the neutral Referee shall be final and binding on all parties to the dispute. The
  fees and charges of such neutral Referee shall be borne equally by the Company and the
  Association.

  5. During the period a grievance is being handled under the provisions of Section 23 (Union
  Security) and until final award by the Vice President-Flight Operations, their designee or the
  neutral Referee, the employee shall not be discharged from the Company nor lose any Seniority
  rights because of non-compliance with the terms and provisions of Section 23 (Union Security).

  1. Establishment. There shall be established a Retirement Board (hereinafter referred to as the

  rules for the selection of the members of the Board to be selected by it and the Association shall

  The Company shall also select one (1) alternate member who may act for either of the two (2)
  members of the Board appointed by the Company in the event of the absence or inability to act of
  one (1) of such members, and the Association shall likewise select one (1) alternate member who
  may act for either of the two (2) members of the Board appointed by the Association in the event
  of the absence or inability to act of one (1) of such members. Either the Company or the
  Association at any time may remove a member appointed by it and may select a member to fill
  any vacancy among the members selected by it. Both the Company and the Association shall, in
  writing, notify each other respectively concerning such selections, which shall continue until
  further written notice.

  3. Quorum and Voting. Three (3) members of the Board shall constitute a quorum for the
  transaction of business. At all Board meetings, Company members present shall be entitled to
  one (1) vote each and Association members present shall be entitled to one (1) vote each. If at any
  such meeting two (2) Company members are not present, the Company member present may cast
  two (2) votes and if two (2) Association members are not present, the Association member
  present may cast two (2) votes.

  members of the Board to handle any problem within the jurisdiction of the Board. Such
  subcommittee(s) shall report exclusively to the Board.

  of the Board selected by the Company which are incidental to the holding of such meetings and

  precipitates the cockpit conflict, and it is brought to the attention of the Professional

  forthright and reasoned manner, in an attempt to settle their dispute in a no-fault

  Committee meeting. After each pilot has had the opportunity to present their view on
  the matter, the Committee will seek a commitment from the parties to end the conflict
  and work together in the future constructively and without dissension.
  4) Should one (1) of the pilots refuse to participate and the issue remains unresolved, the
  Professional Standards Committee will advise the Local Executive Council (LEC)

  or an exemption to FAR 117 as referred to in Section 10.C.3.). Such planned FRMS must be
  specific in nature including, but not limited to, the FAR in question. The purpose of the
  planned FRMS will be stated to the Fatigue Risk Management Team (FRMT) in advance of
  any data collection effort.

  2. The FRMT is a technical body consisting of no more than two members appointed by the
  Association and two members appointed by the Company. The FRMT will:
  a. Advise the Company on matters related to managing the risk of pilot fatigue and
  operations conducted under a FRMS, and
  b. Administer data collection efforts to be conducted by the Company.

  3. A data collection effort must:
  a. Require no onerous, excessive, or unsafe efforts by participants,
  b. Bear a reasonable relationship to the Company’s current or planned operations or
  FAA/PWA flight and duty time rules or regulations, and
  c. Not be inappropriate or unjustified.

  4. A data collection effort may address any of the following:
  a. Patterns of sleep
  b. Alertness
  c. Cognitive performance
  d. Cumulative fatigue
  e. Mood
  f. Circadian rhythm disruption
  g. Quality of crew rest facilities
  h. Rest prior to, during, and following select Flight Groupings
  i. Other matters as determined by the FRMT

  5. The Company will solicit the voluntary participation of pilots in data collection efforts. No
  disciplinary or retaliatory action will be taken against a pilot who chooses not to participate.
  After consultation with the FRMT, the Company may terminate a pilot’s participation in the
  data collection at any time if the Company, the FRMT, or any participating scientists,
  consultants, or advisers determine it is not in the best interest of the pilot to continue
  participation.

QQ.  COMMUTER POLICY

  1. Pilots are expected to exercise prudent judgment and planning to avoid commuting problems, and
  are responsible for reporting for their flight assignment with sufficient time and with adequate
  rest prior to beginning scheduled duty. It is expected that a pilot will rarely utilize the provisions
  of this Commuter Policy.
