2. A pilot must attempt to commute on a minimum of two (2) consecutive scheduled flights (HA or
  OAL), with adequate time between them (e.g., scheduled to depart from different ends of the
  same airport). If, because of flight cancellations, delays, lack of available seating (cabin or
  jumpseat), or delays beyond the commuter’s control (diversion, etc.), the pilot will be unable to
  arrive prior to the scheduled report time, Crew Scheduling shall be notified immediately.

  a. Only one (1) scheduled flight is required if:
  1) The flight is scheduled to arrive prior to the pilot’s report time, and
  2) The pilot has a confirmed ticket on an OAL, or
  3) The flight is operated by HA, and
  a) At twenty-four (24) hours prior to the flight’s scheduled departure:
  (1) The pilot was confirmed for the jumpseat, or
  (2) The flight had more open seats available than the pilot’s standby ranking on the
  non-rev list.

  3. Upon request of the Chief Pilot, the pilot should be prepared to provide supporting documentation
  that they were present for the commuting flight(s).

  4. Pilots who commute by other means (e.g., automobile, train, bus, etc.) shall also be covered under
  this policy for unforeseen events, provided they notify Crew Scheduling as soon as such events
  become known, and their scheduled report time is no longer possible. Examples of such events
  include but are not limited to severe unforecasted weather conditions, traffic, vehicular accidents,
  and mechanical breakdowns.

  5. Pilots utilizing the Commuter Policy who arrive at their domicile after the first Segment of their
  Flight Grouping has departed, or another pilot has been assigned to cover the Flight Grouping, or
  the start of their Reserve Availability Period has commenced, shall be subject to any of the
  following, at the discretion of a Crew Scheduling Duty Manager:

  a. Placed back onto the pilot’s originally scheduled Flight Grouping if the Flight Grouping
  passed through the pilot’s Domicile, or

  b. Assigned to any Flight Grouping (including Interisland Airport Reserve) by mutual
  agreement between the pilot and the Crew Scheduling Duty Manager, or

  c. Removed from the scheduled Flight Grouping or Reserve Availability Period.

  6. The pilot will not receive Pay and Credit for scheduled Segments that are not flown due to the
  utilization of the Commuter Policy.

  7. A commuting pilot who complies with the requirements of this policy shall not be subject to
  discipline based on missed assignments unless there is evidence of a pattern of inadequate
  planning by the pilot. The Chief Pilot may discuss patterns of missed assignments with the pilot
  in an effort to resolve such issues by identifying the source problem and to assist in developing
  alternative commuting strategies. Repeated missed assignments may be considered when
  evaluating whether there is evidence of a pattern of inadequate planning by the pilot.

LETTER OF AGREEMENT
  Between
  THE AIRLINE PILOTS
  In the service of
  HAWAIIAN AIRLINES, INC.
  As represented by
  THE AIR LINE PILOTS ASSOCIATION, INTERNATIONAL

  FLIGHT OPERATIONS QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM

  THIS LETTER OF AGREEMENT is made and entered into in accordance with the provisions of
Title II of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, by and between HAWAIIAN AIRLINES, INC. (hereinafter
referred to as “ the Company” or “Hawaiian Airlines”) and the AIRLINE PILOTS in the service of Hawaiian
Airlines, Inc. as represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International (hereinafter referred to as
“The Association” or “ ALPA”).

  WITNESSETH:

  WHEREAS, it is the intent of the parties to implement a Flight Operations Quality Assurance
Program (FOQA) to analyze data for the sole purpose of enhancing safety , and

  WHEREAS, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) , has implemented FAR 13.401 that
ensures FOQA data from carriers participating in an approved program will not be used to undertake any
enforcement action against an air carrier or its employees, and

  WHEREAS, the parties agree that it is appropriate to initiate a trial FOQA program given the
above assurance and that such trial program will terminate eighteen months from the date of
implementation of the program, unless it is mutually agreed to make this FOQA program a permanent
program.

  Now, THEREFORE, it is mutually agreed as follows:

A.  DEFINITIONS:

  1.  “ Aircraft Condition Monitoring System” or “ Quick Access Recorder (QAR)” means any
  quick-access recorder that captures flight data onto any removable optical disk or any
  equivalent system .

  2.  “Cockpit Voice Recorder” is any device, equipment or system which monitors or records
  a pilot' s voice while he or she is on an aircraft.

  3.  “ Collected Data" is data which has been recorded and removed from an aircraft via a
  data collection device or method for use in the FOQA program.

  4.  “ De-identified Data” means any FOQA data that exists following the deletion and
  destruction of any data that could in any way be used to identify specific crew members.

  5.  “Flight Data Recorder ” is any device , equipment or system which collects, transmits or
  records in-flight data, whether installed to monitor pilot, aircraft component, or aircraft
  performance, or as a consequence of performance of some other function.

  1

6.  “ FOQA Gatekeeper ” is an ALPA member appointed by the Hawaiian Airlines Master
  Executive Council (HAL MEC) , who alone has been authorized as the sole individual to
  have access to FOQA information which would allow the identification of a crew member
  associated with collected data, as well as sole authorization to retrieve such information
  from the computer to view Identifying Data before de-identification , or to obtain the
  identity of crew members after an Operational Exceedance Event , or to contact such
  crew members to obtain additional information for use by the FOQA program. The HAL
  MEC will also appoint an alternate FOQA Gatekeeper who, in coordination with the
  FOQA Gatekeeper, shall perform the duties of the FOQA Gatekeeper pursuant to this
  paragraph in the event the FOQA Gatekeeper is unavailable.

7.  "FOQA Monitoring Team” ( FMT) means a committee composed of the FOQA Program
  Manager, the Vice President of Flight Operations , a Chief Pilot , the Fleet Captain of each
  aircraft fleet , the ALPA Central Air Safety Committee Chairman , the ALPA Gatekeeper ,
  the Safety Department FOQA Analyst , a Maintenance & Engineering Department
  representative and a Flight Operations Engineering representative . This Team will
  review aggregate trend data to identify safety concerns and provide recommendations to
  stakeholders. Decision making within the FMT will be conducted on a consensus basis.

8.  “FOQA Program” is a program designed to enhance flight safety through controlled
  analysis of recorded flight data information .

9.  “FOQA Program Manager” - The Director of Safety will serve as the FOQA Program
  Manager and is responsible for the overall management , administration , security and
  maintenance of the FOQA program .

10 .  “ FOQA Steering Committee” (FSC) is chaired by the Director of Safety and serves as the
  advisory group for the FOQA program . Members of this committee include the following :
  Senior Vice President of Operations , the Vice President of Flight Operations, the Vice
  President of Maintenance & Engineering , the Senior Fleet Captain, and the Air Line Pilots
  Association Master Executive Council Chairman. The FSC will normally meet semi-
  annually.

11.  " Identified Data” is any recorded or collected flight data prior to removal of all identifying
  data.

12 .  “Identifying Data” is any data or combination of data which allows recorded or collected
  flight data to be associated with a specific crew member .

13 .  “ Information” is any data transmitted , recorded or collected by use of a flight data
  recorder , cockpit voice recorder or any other recording device. The term “Information”
  shall further include tapes, transcripts, reports , papers, memos, statements, studies ,
  charts, graphs or any other description , analysis or compilation of data collected by any
  such equipment.

14.  “ Operational Exceedance Event” - An event , as determined by recorded data, indicating
  that an aircraft was in a situation outside of the normal agreed-upon flight operations
  envelope tolerances.

15 .  “ Operational Routine Event” - An event in routine operation of statistical interest.

16 .  “ Safety Department FOQA Analyst” is a company safety department representative
  tasked with review of processed de-identified FOQA data returned to Hawaiian Airlines
  by the vendor. The FOQA Analyst does not have access to identifying data except as
  provided by the ALPA Gatekeeper.

B  FOQA PROGRAM

  1.  The design, implementation, and operation of a FOQA program shall be by mutual
  agreement between the Company and the Air Line Pilots Association. Any variation from
  the agreed-upon FOQA program shall require the mutual agreement of the parties prior
  to implementation . The parties shall mutually agree in writing to an implementation date
  for the FOQA program. The agreed upon implementation date shall be used to
  determine the duration of the FOQA Program trial period provided for in paragraph G .
  herein .

  2.  The FMT shall establish necessary policies and procedures to ensure compliance with
  the provisions of this agreement.

  3.  The design of the FOQA program shall maintain the confidentiality and anonymity of
  individual crew members .

  4  Any violation of the requirements of the agreed-upon FOQA program, or the terms
  herein, shall be cause for an immediate suspension of all FOQA data collection until such
  time as a review of the violation has been conducted between the parties. In the event of
  such suspension , any collected data which has not yet been de-identified shall be
  destroyed. The suspension will continue until such time as the parties are satisfied that
  the problem has been rectified . Notwithstanding the forgoing, if a party feels that its
  interests are no longer protected as set forth in this document , the program may be
  terminated and all identified data shall be immediately destroyed pursuant to Paragraph
  G. 3 herein below.

  5.  At a minimum, the FOQA program at Hawaiian Airlines will record, examine and monitor
  the exceedances listed in FAA Advisory Circular AC120-82 , Appendix II.

  6.  The establishment of the limits which define an exceedance will be determined by the
  Company ’s Flight Standards and Training Department. Such exceedance limits shall be
  subject to review and require approval of the FOQA Monitoring Team.

c.  SCOPE

  1.  Sufficient de-identified data shall be maintained to fulfill the requirements of the agreed-
  upon FOQA program . All de-identified data, and analyses of such data, shall be made
  available upon request to the parties including the HAL MEC.

  2.  There shall be continual evaluation of exceedance values by the parties and all changes,
  deletions, or additions will be approved by the FMT .

  3.  The FAA will be provided the opportunity to review de-identified, trend analysis and
  corrective action plans on company property during regularly scheduled briefings as
  provided for in AC 120-82.

  3

D.  DATA RETENTION AND SECURITY

  1.  Identifying data shall be removed from identified data as soon as possible, and shall be
  destroyed no later than fourteen (14) calendar days from the date of retrieval of the data
  by the Company.

  2.  All FOQA information identified , or de-identified, is Hawaiian Airlines proprietary
  information and shall be treated as confidential. No information obtained from or by use
  of this program shall be released except as stated in paragraphs D. 3 through D . 6 .

  3.  Any employee/agent who has contact with any identified data used in this FOQA program
  shall be prohibited from divulging any identifying data to any individual other than the
  designated FOQA Gatekeeper. In the event any employee/agent divulges any identifying
  data to any individual other than the designated FOQA Gatekeeper, such
  employee/agent shall immediately be removed from contact with any FOQA data,
  identified or de-identified, at least until such time as an investigation on such divulgence
  is concluded and the parties are satisfied that the situation is adequately resolved .
  Nothing in this Paragraph precludes either party from exercising the provisions of
  Paragraph B. 4 above .

  4.  Except as required pursuant to Paragraph D.5, the release of identified data without
  expressed written consent of both parties is strictly prohibited . If either party discovers an
  unauthorized release they shall immediately notify the other party. The unauthorized
  release shall be immediately investigated and corrective action taken to protect all
  crewmembers, the Company, and the Association, and to prevent additional release of
  data and/or Information. It is expressly understood that the timely investigation of an
  unauthorized release of data as set forth in this paragraph shall be conducted prior to
  either party’s demand for termination of the FOQA Program as set forth in paragraph B. 4
  of this agreement.

  5.  In the event either party is requested or required (by oral question, interrogatories,
  requests for information or documents, subpoena, civil investigative demand, or similar
  process) to disclose any identified data or de-identified data, that party will promptly notify
  the other party of such request or requirement and an appropriate protective order shall
  be sought. If a party is compelled by court order to disclose identified data or de-
  identified data that party may disclose only such of the identified data or de-identified
  data as is required by law and such disclosure shall be limited to the party compelling
  disclosure.

  6.  Except as required under Paragraph D. 5 , the release of de-identified data to a third party
  is not authorized without the express approval of both the FOQA Manager and the FOQA
  Gatekeeper, except that such approval is not required in the case of the FAA pursuant to
  paragraph C.3 above. In any case, the FMT shall be advised of and provided a copy of
  any de-identified data released to any third party.

  7.  Only the FOQA Gatekeeper shall be issued a Crypto Card which allows access to
  identified data. It is the FOQA Gatekeeper’s responsibility to safeguard this Crypto Card
  and the password associated with that card.

E.  DATA USE

  1.  The sole contact with any flight crew member associated with a specific exceedance
  event shall be through the designated FOQA Gatekeeper.

1. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in Section 1.B. of the Pilots’
Agreement, the Company shall be permitted to engage in the Code Sharing Agreement for a

2. For purposes of this Letter of Agreement, a “Code Share Related Market” is a set
of two or more airports between which passengers may book itineraries that
include a segment operated by China Airlines using the HA or HA* code as
described in paragraph 1. above.

Examples:

(i) A passenger may book an itinerary under the Company designator code from

segment and Company aircraft for AKL-HNL. BNE-HNL and BNE-AKL
are each a Code Share Related Market.

3. On a quarterly basis, the Company shall present to ALPA an analysis of the
profitability of using Company aircraft to fly in Code Share Related Markets
identified by ALPA, provided that each Code Share Related Market identified by
ALPA is one in which there is a per flight average, computed over the preceding
quarter, of at least one hundred and twenty (120) passengers on a flight segment
flown to or from HNL whose itinerary includes a particular flight on a China

The Company will provide to ALPA, on a confidential basis, information
necessary to determine whether the passenger threshold has been met in any Code
Share Related Market in any quarter.

4, “Profitability” under paragraph 3 above means that it can be predicted with
reasonable certainty that the Company can begin flying with its own aircraft
between two airports in a Code Share Related Market, at least one of which is not
then served by the Company, and, taking into account the revenues, if any, earned

investment capital and (b) recover its cumulative investment including start-up
losses on the Code Share Related Market within a period of seventy (70) months.

initiating service in the Code Share Related Market on the Company’s existing
market (e.g., in evaluating BKK-HNL, the Company may consider the impact of

information provided in such analysis or provided under paragraph 3 above.

5. If a dispute arises as to whether a Code Share Related Market satisfies the
passenger threshold in paragraph 3, above, or the profitability test in paragraph 4
above, that dispute shall be subject to final and binding, expedited arbitration
before the ALPA-Hawaiian System Board of Adjustment sitting with Donald
Munroe as the neutral member (or, in his absence, with another neutral member
jointly selected by the Parties).

6. If a Code Share Related Market satisfies the profitability test in paragraph 4
above, the Parties shall meet within ninety (90) days to discuss the following
options: (a) that the Code Sharing Agreement continue without. Company
operation in the Code Share Related Market; (b) that the Company should begin
service in the Code Share Related Market with its own aircraft, or (c) that the
Company should cease placing the HA or HA* code on the China Airlines
segment of the Code Share Related Market (e.g. BKK-TPE).

7. If there is no agreement on option 6(a) above, then the Company must either: (a)
at the next regularly scheduled meeting of the Board of Directors, seek and obtain
Board approval to commence service in the Code Share Related Market with the
Company’s own aircraft within a further six (6) month period of time; or (b)
within the same period cease placing the HA or HA* code on the China Airlines
segment of the Code Share Related Market.

8. If any other dispute arises under this Letter of Agreement, that dispute shall be
subject to final and binding expedited arbitration before the ALPA-Hawaiian
System Board of Adjustment sitting with Donald Munroe as the neutral member
(or, in his absence, with another neutral member jointly selected by the Parties).

9. This Letter of Agreement shall be effective as of the date of execution stated
below, and shall remain in effect concurrently with the Pilots’ Agreement and in
accordance with Section 28, Duration.

10. This Letter of Agreement applies only to the China Airlines Code Sharing
Agreement and not to any other code sharing agreement and it may apply to
future code sharing agreements only to the extent that the Parties agree.

  PROCESS (“UFAP”)
  1. All ULCC Reserve pilots shall be divided into “buckets” based on the number of days
  they have remaining in their current block of Reserve days.

  2. Any uncovered Flight Groupings will be assigned during the OTSL/UFAP process to the
  first ULCR pilot in the bucket that matches the number of days covered by the Flight
  Grouping (e.g., two-day (2-day) Flight Grouping shall be assigned to the first ULCR pilot
  in the 2-day bucket).

  a. Bucket Assignment Order (BAO) shall be based upon the projected credit value each
  pilot within a specific bucket has at the time of call out or notification. Pilots shall be
  listed in the appropriate call out order within their respective buckets starting with the
  lowest credit and ending with the highest credit. The pilot with the lowest credit value
  that is legal for the Flight Grouping within each bucket shall be assigned first,
  respecting all relevant legalities and eligibilities, including RAPs.

access recorder that captures flight data onto any removable memory card or equivalent system to f
include data transfer via electronic means. :

Company.

collection device or method, for use in the FOQA program.

any data that could in any way be used to identify specific crew members.

  23-11 Freight Implementation and Deadhead Operations

THIS LETTER OF AGREEMENT (“LOA”) is made and entered into in accordance with the
provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, by and between HAWAIIAN AIRLINES,
INC (hereinafter referred to as the “Company”) and the air line pilots in the service of the
Company, as represented by the AIR LINE PILOTS ASSOCIATION (hereinafter referred to as
the “Association”).

WHEREAS, the Company and the Association are parties to a collective bargaining agreement
setting forth the rates of pay, rules, and working conditions for the Company’s pilots (“Pilot
Working Agreement” or “PWA”), effective March 2, 2023, and

WHEREAS, due to the scheduled operating hours of the new Freight Operation it necessitated
the ability to conduct IOE on “red-eye” Segments, and
WHEREAS, both parties saw a need to change the timeline for booking travel to and from
training, and the ability to schedule pilots for IOE without returning them to Domicile first, and
WHEREAS, the Company saw a need to Deadhead a Freight Pilot on a freight aircraft to reduce
the delay of a departure, while both parties agree that the reduction of costs shall not be a reason
to utilize freight aircraft to Deadhead Freight Pilots, and
WHEREAS, both parties saw a need to allow a Long Call Reserve Freight Pilot the ability to
utilize the Freight Pilot Commuter Allowance, and
NOW, THEREFORE, the Company and Association agree as follows:

A. IOE during Red-eye Flights
  1. Subparagraph 9.H.4 shall be changed to read:
  a. Flight Groupings containing an un-augmented “red-eye” Segment or Flight
  Groupings that include destinations not listed as “Approved IOE Segments” in that
  Month’s Notification of Bidding Period for Monthly Runs Bulletin shall not be
  utilized for conducting IOE.
  1) Subparagraph 9.H.4 shall not apply to Freight Operations

B.  Travel to and from Simulator (both Students and IE pilots)
  1. Subparagraph 9.S.8.b shall read:

a. Travel to training on a non-Hawaiian Airlines flight shall be booked, and pilot

  a. Travel from training on a non-Hawaiian Airlines flight shall be booked, and pilot
  notified, no later than five (5) days prior to the pilot’s return travel day.
  3. Paragraph E of LOA 23-10 Training and Freight shall be changed to read:
  b. Training Travel Deviation
  1) Location: The pilot may choose to depart from a location other than their
  Domicile if airfare cost is less than the airfare (determined by HA cost) to/from
  the pilot’s Domicile at time of booking. In addition, the deviation must allow the
  pilot to legally complete their next assignment. Subparagraph 7.A.6-8 does not
  apply to a training travel Deviation. The pilot must provide notice fourteen (14)
  days prior to their first travel day. DH Pay and/or Credit will be calculated in

  2) Non-utilization: If the pilot is not going to utilize the travel to training, the pilot
  should notify the Company to cancel their segment(s) fourteen (14) days prior to

  traveled on the scheduled travel training day(s) to/from their Domicile.

C.  Deadheading Greater than 5.5 hours on OAL
  1. Subparagraph 7.A.8.a.7) (to be added after the existing language) “If an aisle or window
  seat in the next highest product are not available, the pilot shall be assigned an aisle, then
  window, seat in the highest class.”
  2. Pilots may waive deadhead provisions as long as they are provided clear, mutually agreed
  information (ALPA-approved script) regarding their contractual right for a Deadhead,
  and such waiver is recorded for potential verification at a later date.

D. IOE
  1. Subparagraph 9.H.7 shall read:
  b. The Company is not required to Deadhead pilots in training back to their Domicile
  between completion of simulator training and their first IOE Flight Grouping, or
  FAM flight, if there are less than four (4) calendar days between the conclusion of
  simulator training and the IOE Flight Grouping. If a pilot is scheduled for two (2)

  their current Domicile, and less than four (4) calendar days off exist between the
  ending of the first Flight Grouping and the beginning of the second Flight Grouping,
  the Company is not required to Deadhead the pilot back to their current Domicile
  between IOE Flight Groupings.
  1) Upon Completion of IOE, the pilot will either be activated in the Category or, if
  the pilot qualifies for a move, the pilot shall be Deadheaded back to Domicile.
  2) Pilots shall be provided hotel, per diem, and transportation during the time period
  away from Domicile, as well as the three (3) hours per day required per PWA

  1. Subsection 7.D shall read:
  a. The Company may Deadhead a Freight Pilot on a freight aircraft only if the Freight

  1) is unable to be in position utilizing commercial flights and/or ground

THIS LETTER OF AGREEMENT (“LOA”) is made and entered into in accordance with the
provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, by and between HAWAIIAN AIRLINES,
INC (hereinafter referred to as the “Company”) and the air line pilots in the service of the
Company, as represented by the AIR LINE PILOTS ASSOCIATION (hereinafter referred to as
the Association”),
WHEREAS, the Company and the Association are parties to a collective bargaining agreement
setting forth the rates of pay, rules, and working conditions for the Company’s pilots (“Pilots’
Working Agreement” or “PWA”) effective March 2, 2023; and
WHEREAS, the parties had not anticipated all possible staffing scenarios when contemplating
the language regarding the calculation of the Minimum Reserve Number (“MRN”); and
WHEREAS, it was in the best interest of both parties to modify how the MRN shall be
calculated going forward.
NOW, THEREFORE, the Company and Association agree as follows:
Subsection 21.H shall be changed to read:
H. MINIMUM RESERVE NUMBER (MRN
1. Once the Bid Award process is complete, the Minimum Reserve Number (MRN) for each
calendar day will be determined for the month. The MRN shall be calculated as follows:
a. The net reserve number for a given calendar day is the number of awarded Reserve
pilots for that day, minus the number of uncovered Flight Groupings in open time
operating that day.
b. The MRN shall be the lesser of the net reserve number or the PRN for that day,
reduced by one for every fifty (50) eligible bid pilots in that Category, rounded up to
the next multiple of fifty (50).
Example: The PRN for a given day is 18. There are 15 net reserves following the Bid
Award process on the same given day, in a Category with 80 eligible bid pilots. The
next multiple of 50 above 80 is 100, so the net reserve number will be reduced by two.
The MRN will be 13 for that day.

1) On the following named holidays, the MRN shall not be reduced by the formula
in Subparagraph 21.H.1.b, and shall instead be equal to the lesser of the net
reserve number or the PRN:

a) New Year’s Day

2. Reserve coverage for each day in the month will be determined by subtracting the
number of uncovered Flight Groupings in open time that are operating on a given day
from the number of available reserves on that day, and comparing the resulting number of
net reserves to the MRN for that day.
a. Ifthe number of net reserves exceeds the MRN, the reserve grid on that day will have
net positive reserve coverage and be considered “green.”
b. Ifthe number of net reserves is equal to or less than the MRN, the reserve grid on that
day will be “black.”

ARTICLE 1
ESTABLISHMENT OF PLAN

Effective June 1, 1949, Hawaiian Airlines, Inc. established a Retirement Income
Plan for its eligible employees. Benefits under the Plan for Pilot employees had been
funded under Group Annuity Contract No. GA-9006 issued to the Company by the
Prudential Insurance Company of America.

Effective March 20, 1963, said Retirement Income Plan, formerly embodied in
the provisions of Contract 9006, was amended and restated in its entirety, with respect
to employees in the employ of the Company on that date who were classified as Pilots
and who were not receiving annuity payments, and as to future employees of the
Company classified as Pilots, and as to alt benefits for which such employees are
entitled under the Retirement Income Plan.

Effective January 1,1971 Contract 9006 was amended to provide for the
cancellation of all retirement income benefits credited thereunder before March 20,1963
to the employees described above. All amounts arising as a result of such cancellation
were transferred to a new deposit administration Group Annuity Contract No. GA-9102
issued to the Company by Prudential. All benefits under the Retirement Income Plan, as
amended and restated, was provided under Contract 9102.

Effective March 1, 1975, the Plan was renamed the Retirement Plan for Pilots of
Hawaiian Airlines, Inc. and amended and restated in its entirety to meet the
requirements of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended.

The Plan was amended and restated in its entirety as of January 1, 1994, which
restatement was amended from time to time thereafter. The Plan was amended and
restated in its entirety as of January 1, 1997, which restatement was amended from time
to time thereafter. The Plan was amended and restated in its entirety effective
January 1, 2007 to reflect certain collectively bargained changes to the Plan, including
the freeze of Plan benefit accruals for certain pilots. This restatement was amended
from time to time thereafter.

Effective as of January 1, 2015, the Plan is hereby amended and restated in its
entirety to incorporate all prior amendments and amendments required by changes in
the laws and regulations affecting the Plan. All such amendments shall be effective on
the applicable effective date of such laws with respect to employees in the employ of the
Company on or after the effective date who are classified as Pilots and with respect to
future employees of the Company classified as Pilots.

Effective March 1, 1975, the Variable Plan, which had been in effect since
May 1,1956, was terminated. A valuation of the Variable Plan’s assets was made as of
March 31,1975. On the basis of this valuation, an index of change was developed by a
comparison of the market value of the assets as of December 31, 1974. This index of
change was used to adjust the Pilots’ Contribution Accounts as well as determining a
new annuity unit value for those retired under this Plan.

The trustee continued to pay the Variable Plan pensions through July 1975 in the
same amount as were being paid in June 1975. The Retired Members had their
Variable Plan pension paid from Prudential beginning August 1, 1975. The amount of
the Variable Plan pension payable to eligible Retired Members on August 1,1975 was
the amount which would have been paid to each such Member on July 1,1975 based on
the December 31, 1974 annuity unit value, adjusted by the index of changes as
mentioned above. The amount of each such annuity was expressed in terms of Annuity
Units of Variable Annuity determined by multiplying the dollar amount of such August 1,
1975 payment by the Annuity Units Per Dollar for August 1, 1975. The number of
Annuity Units per Dollar for August 1975 was equal to $1.00 divided by the Annuity Unit
Value applicable to annuity payments made in such month. “Annuity Unit Value” is
described in the following paragraph. The amount of each subsequent monthly Variable
Plan pension payment was equal to the product of the number of Annuity Units
constituting such monthly payment and the Annuity Unit Value applicable to annuity
payments in such month. (The dollar amount of each such payment fluctuates each
monih as the Annuity Unit Value fluctuates in dollar value).

The Annuity Unit Value is based on the effective investment results, including
market value changes and dividends, less investment expenses and taxes and an
assumed investment result, of an investment fund composed primarily of common
stocks. The method of valuing this Annuity Unit Value is determined in accordance with
the group annuity contract or contracts issued by Prudential to the Company.

The assets supporting the Variable-Pian which are not transferred to purchase
pensions for those retired and vested as Pilots, and are not transferred as Pilot
contributions, remained with the trustee and are used as part of the assets of this Plan.

HAWAIIAN AIRLINES, INC.
PILOTS’ 401(K) PLAN

WHEREAS, Hawaiian Airlines, Inc. established a savings plan, effective
September 1, 1990, known as the Hawaiian Airlines, Inc. Pilots' 401(k) Plan (the
"Plan") to enable the employees of Hawaiian Airlines, Inc. who are covered by a
collective bargaining agreement with the Air Line Pilots Association, International
to make tax-deferred salary reduction contributions; and

WHEREAS, the Plan has been amended from time to time and must be
amended to reflect changes agreed to by collective bargaining;

NOW THEREFORE, it is hereby agreed that effective as of May 1, 2007,
the Hawaiian Airlines, Inc. Pilots’ 401(k) Plan is amended and restated in its
entirety to read as herein provided.

ARTICLE 1
NAME AND PURPOSE
1.1. NAME. The Plan shall be known as the Hawaiian Airlines, Inc. Pilots’
401(k) Plan.
1.2 PURPOSE.

(A) Provision for Participants' Economic Security. The purpose of the
Plan is to receive contributions on behalf of Participants and to assist Participants
in providing for their future economic security.

(B) Qualification as Profit Sharing Plan With a Cash or Deferred
Arrangement. The Plan is intended to qualify as a profit sharing plan under
Section 401(a) of the Code, including a cash or deferred arrangement under
Section 401(k) of the Code.

(C) Exclusive Benefit of Participants. The Plan and the Trust shall be
administered for the exclusive benefit of the Participants and their Beneficiaries
and shall not be used for or diverted to any other purposes.

ARTICLE 2
DEFINITIONS

For the purposes of this Plan, unless the context requires otherwise, the
following words and phrases, when used herein with initial capital letters, shall
have the meanings indicated.

2.1 ACCOUNTS. With respect to any Participant, the aggregate of all of the
accounts established and maintained on his behalf under the Plan, which
accounts may include a Salary Deferral Account, Roth Deferral Account, Target
Benefit Account, Defined Contribution Account, Regular Rollover Account, Roth
Rollover Account, Employer Stock Contribution Account, and Voluntary After Tax
Contribution Account.
2.2 ACTUAL DEFERRAL PERCENTAGE (ADP). For a specified group of
participants (either Highly Compensated Employees or Non-highly Compensated
Employees) for a Plan Year, the average of the ratios (calculated separately for
each Participant in such group) of (i) the amount of Employer contributions actually
paid over to the Trust on behalf of such Participant for the Plan Year to (ii) the
Participant's Statutory Compensation for such Plan Year. Employer contributions
on behalf of any Participant shall include any Elective Deferrals (other than Catch-
up Contributions) made pursuant to the Participant's deferral election (including
Excess Elective Deferrals of Highty Compensated Employees), but excluding (i)
Excess Elective Deferrals of Non-highiy Compensated Employees that arise solely
from Elective Deferrals made under this Plan or other plans of the Employer and
(ii) Elective Deferrals that are taken into account in the Actual Contribution
Percentage test (provided the ADP test is satisfied both with and without exclusion
of these elective deferrals). For purposes of computing Actual Deferral
Percentages, an Employee who would be a Participant but for the failure to make
Elective Deferrals shall be treated as a Participant on whose behalf no Elective
Deferrals are made.
2.3. ALTERNATE PAYEE. Any spouse, former spouse, child, or other
dependent of a Participant who is recognized by a Qualified Domestic Relations
Order as having a right to receive all, or a portion of, the benefits payable under
the Plan with respect to such Participant.
2.4 ASSOCIATION. The Air Line Pilots Association, International.
2.55 AVERAGE ACTUAL DEFERRAL PERCENTAGE. The average
(expressed as a percentage) of the Actual Deferral Percentages of the
Participants in a group.
2.6 BENEFICIARY. Any person designated by a Participant in accordance with
Article 9 to receive any sums payable hereunder if such Person survives the
Participant.
2.7 CATCH-UP CONTRIBUTIONS. Elective Deferrals made to the Plan that
are in excess of an otherwise applicable Plan limit and that are made by a
Participant who is aged 50 or over by the end of his taxable year. An otherwise
applicable Plan limit is a limit in the Plan that applies to Elective Deferrals without
regard to Catch-up Contributions, such as the limits on Annual Additions, the dollar

limitation on Elective Deferrals under Section 402(g) of the Code (not counting
Catch-up Contributions), and the limit imposed by the Actual Deferral Percentage
test under Section 401(k)(3) of the Code. Catch-up Contributions for a Participant
for a taxable year may not exceed the dollar limit on Catch-up Contributions under
Section 414(v)(2)(B)(i) of the Code for the taxable year. The dollar limit on Catch-
up Contributions under Section 414(v)(2)(B)(i) of the Code is $5,000 for taxable
years beginning in 2006 and later years. After 2006, the $5,000 limit shall be
adjusted by the Secretary of the Treasury for cost-of-living increases under Section
414(v)(2(c) of the Code. Catch-up Contributions shall not be subject to the limits
on Annual Additions, shail not be counted in the Actual Deferral Percentage test,
and shall not be counted in determining the minimum allocation under Section 416
of the Code (but Catch-up Contributions made in prior years shall be counted in
determining whether the Plan is top-heavy).

2.8 CODE. The Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, and all rules,
rulings, and regulations thereunder.

2.9 COMPENSATION. The total amount of compensation paid to a Participant :
by the Employer during a Plan Year as reflected on the Form W-2 filed by the
Employer with respect to such Participant for the Plan Year plus any Elective
Deferrals authorized by the Participant under this Plan and any amount that is
contributed by the Employer pursuant to a Elective Deferral agreement and is not
includible in the Participant's gross income under Section 125, 132(f)(4), 402(e)(3),
402(h)(1)(B), and 403(b). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Compensation shall not
include cash profit bonus payments.

For Plan Years beginning before January 1, 1995, the Compensation of
each Participant taken into account for determining all benefits provided under the
Plan for any Plan Year shall not exceed $200,000 (hereinafter the "$200,000
limitation"). For each such Plan Year, this limitation shall be adjusted by the
Secretary of the Treasury at the same time and in the same manner as under
Section 415(d) of the Code, except that the dollar increase in effect on January 1
of any calendar year shall be effective for the Plan Year beginning in such
calendar year and the first adjustment to the $200,000 limitation shall be effective
on January 1, 1990.

For Plan Years beginning on or after January 1, 1995 and before
January 1, 2002, the annual Compensation of each Participant taken into account
for determining all benefits provided under the Plan for any Plan Year shall not
exceed $150,000, as adjusted for increases in the cost-of-living in accordance with
Section 401(a)(17)(B) of the Code. The cost-of-living adjustment in effect for a
calendar year shall apply to any determination period beginning in such calendar
year.

For Plan Years beginning after December 31, 2001, the annual

17.1. CLAIMS AND DETERMINATION.

(A) Any claim for benefits under this Plan shall be in writing to the Plan
Administrator.

(B) (1) Ifaclaim is denied in whole or in part, the Plan Administrator
shall give the claimant written notice of such denial within a reasonable period of
time, but not later than 90 days after receipt of the claim, unless the Plan
Administrator determines that special circumstances require an extension of time
for processing the claim. If the Plan Administrator determines that an extension
of time for processing is required, written notice of the extension shall be
furnished to the claimant prior to the termination of the initial 90-day period. In
no event shall such extension exceed a period of 90 days from the end of such
initial period. The extension notice shall indicate the special circumstances
requiring an extension of time and the date by which the Plan Administrator
expects to render the benefit determination.

(2) | The Plan Administrator shall provide the claimant with
written or electronic notification of any adverse benefit determination. Such
notice shall set forth in a manner calculated to be understood by the claimant (i)
the specific reason or reasons for the adverse determination, (ii) reference to the
specific Plan provisions on which the determination is based, (iii) a description of
any additional material or information necessary to perfect the claim and an
explanation of why such material or information is necessary, and (iv) a
description of the review procedure described in Section 17.2 hereof, including a
statement of the claimant's right to bring a civil action under Section 502(a) of
the Act following an adverse benefit determination on review.

21.1. PLAN TERMINATION. The Employer and the Association contemplate that
the Plan and the Trust shall be permanent. Nevertheless, in recognition of the fact
that future conditions and circumstances cannot now be entirely foreseen, the
Employer and the Association reserve the right to terminate either or both the Plan
and the Trust by joint agreement.
21.2 DISCONTINUANCE OF CONTRIBUTIONS. Whenever the Employer and
the Association determine that it is impossible or inadvisable to make further

the Trust, to permanently or temporarily discontinue all further contributions under
the Plan. The Plan Administrator and the Trustee shall thereafter continue to
administer all the provisions of the Plan which are necessary to remain in force,
other than the provisions relating to contributions.
21.3 VESTING UPON TERMINATION AND DISCONTINUANCE. Upon the
termination or partial termination of the Plan or the complete discontinuance of
contributions by the Employer, the rights of each Participant to the amount credited
to his Accounts at such date shall be entirely nonforfeitable without reference to
any formal action on the part of the Employer, the Plan Administrator, or the
Trustee.
21.4 MERGER, CONSOLIDATION, OR SALE. In the event of a merger,
consolidation, or sale of assets of the Employer, under circumstances in which a
successor shall continue and carry on all or a substantial part of the business of
such Employer, and such successor shall employ a substantial number of
Employees of such Employer, then such successor shall carry on the provisions of
this Plan and such successor shall be substituted for the Employer under the
terms and provisions of this Plan.
21.5 VESTED RIGHTS NOT REDUCED ON MERGER, CONSOLIDATION, OR
SALE. Neither the Plan nor the Trust may be merged or consolidated with, nor
may its assets or liabilities be transferred to, any other plan or trust, unless (a) by
joint agreement of the Employer and the Association and (b) each Participant
would (if the Plan then terminated) receive a benefit immediately after the merger,
consolidation, or transfer that is equal to or greater than the benefit he would have
been entitled to receive immediately before the merger, consolidation, or transfer
(if the Plan had then terminated).
21.6 AMENDMENT.

(1) The Employer and the Association may amend the Plan and the
Trust at any time, and from time to time, by joint agreement. No such amendment,
however, shall have the effect of reducing any then nonforfeitable benefits of any
Participant. If the vesting schedule under Article 6 shall be amended and such
amendment would, at any time, decrease the percentage of nonforfeitable benefits
which any Participant would have been entitled to receive had the vesting
schedule not been so amended, then each Participant who is employed on the
date such amendment is adopted, or the date such amendment is effective,
whichever is later, and who has a nonforfeitable right to amounts in his Accounts
pursuant to Article 6 as of the end of the period within which such Participant may
make the election provided for herein, shall be permitted, beginning on the date
such amendment is adopted, to irrevocably elect to have his nonforfeitable interest
computed without regard to such amendment. Written notice of such amendment

LOANS

22.1 SEPARATE LOAN PROCEDURES. A Participant may apply for a loan

include procedures for a Participant who has accounts in more than one defined

for a Participant during the time period that such Participant is on leave due to
qualified military service as permitted under Section 414(u)(4) of the Code. Upon
a Participant's reemployment with the Employer, loan payments shall resume in an
amount which is necessary to provide for level amortization of the entire amount
then outstanding on the loan, over a loan repayment period equal to the original
loan repayment period extended by the length of the qualified military service, or
such longer period as may be allowed by applicable law. With respect to a
Participant who fails to be reemployed with the Employer prior to expiration of
reemployment rights under the Uniformed Services Employment and
Reemployment Rights Act of 1994, the provisions of Section 22.3 shall apply.

WITHDRAWALS
23.1 HARDSHIP WITHDRAWALS. Distribution of Elective Deferrals may be
made on account of financial hardship if the distribution is necessary in light of the
immediate and heavy financial needs of the Participant. Such a distribution shall
not exceed the amount required to meet the immediate financial need created by
the hardship and may not be made to the extent that other financial resources of
the Participant are reasonably available.

(A)  Adistribution shall be deemed to be made on account of the
immediate and heavy financial needs of the Participant if and only if the distribution
is used for the following expenses: _

(1) medical expenses, as defined in Section 213(d) of the Code,
of the Participant or his spouse or dependents;

(2) purchase of a principal residence for the Participant,
excluding mortgage payments;

(3) provide mortgage payments needed to prevent the eviction of
the Participant from, or foreclosure on the mortgage for, the principal residence for
the Participant;

(4) tuition for the next 12 months of post-secondary education for
the Participant or his spouse, children, or dependents.

(5) payments for funeral or burial expenses for the Participant's
deceased parent, spouse, child, or dependent; and

(6) expenses to repair damage to the Participant's principal
residence that would qualify for a casualty loss deduction under Section 165 of the
Code (determined without regard to whether the loss exceeds ten percent of
adjusted gross income).

accordance with written procedures that are established by the Plan Administrator

: Appendix 1
MINIMUM DISTRIBUTION REQUIREMENTS
Section 1. General Rules.

(A) The requirements of this Appendix 1 shall apply to any distribution of
a Participant's interest and shall take precedence over any inconsistent provisions
of this Plan.

(B) All distributions required under Appendix 1 shall be determined and
made in accordance with the regulations under Section 401(a)(9) of the Code and
the minimum distribution incidental benefit requirement of Section 401(a)(9)(G) of
the Code.

(C) As of the first distribution calendar year, distributions to a Participant
shall be made in a single-sum equal to the entire balance of his Accounts.
Section 2. Time and Manner of Distribution.

(A) Required Beginning Date. The Participant's entire interest shall be
distributed to the Participant no later than the Participant's required beginning date.

(B) Death of Participant Before Distributions Begin. If the Participant
dies before distributions begin, the Participant's entire interest shall be distributed
no later than as follows:

(1) If the Participant's surviving spouse is the Participant's sole
designated beneficiary, then distributions to the surviving spouse shall begin by
December 31 of the calendar year immediately following the calendar year in
which the Participant died, or by December 31 of the calendar year in which the
Participant would have attained age 70 1/2, if later.

(2) If the Participant's surviving spouse is not the Participant's
sole designated beneficiary, then distributions to the designated beneficiary shall
begin by December 31 of the calendar year immediately following the calendar
year in which the Participant died.

(3) If there is no designated beneficiary as of September 30 of
the year following the year of the Participant's death, the Participant's entire
interest shall be distributed by December 31 of the calendar year containing the
fifth anniversary of the Participant's death.

(4) If the Participant's surviving spouse is the Participant's sole
designated beneficiary and the surviving spouse dies after the Participant but
before distributions to the surviving spouse are required to begin, this Section 2(B),

(C) Forms of Distribution. Unless the Participant's interest is distributed in a
single-sum on or before the required beginning date, as of the first distribution
calendar year distributions shall be made in accordance with sections 3 and 4 of
this Appendix 1.

Section 3. Required Minimum Distributions During Participant's Lifetime.

(A) Amount of Required Minimum Distribution For Each Distribution
Calendar Year. During the Participant's lifetime, the minimum amount that shall be
distributed for each distribution calendar year shall be the Participant's entire
balance of his Accounts that has not been previously distributed, if any.

(B) Lifetime Required Minimum Distributions Continue Through Year of
Participant's Death. Required minimum distributions shall be determined under
this Section 3 beginning with the first distribution calendar year and continuing up
to, and including, the distribution calendar year that includes the Participant's date
of death.

Section 4. Required Minimum Distributions After Participant's Death.

(A) Death On or After Date Distributions Begin. If the Participant dies on
or after the date distributions begin, the remaining portion of his Accounts, if any,
shall be distributed in a single sum to his Beneficiary determined in accordance
with Article 9.

(B) Death Before Date Distributions Begin. If the Participant dies before
the date distributions begin, the remaining portion of his Accounts, if any, shall be
distributed in a single sum to his Beneficiary determined in accordance with Article
9.

Section 5. Definitions.

(A) Designated beneficiary: The individual who is designated by the
Participant (or the Participant's surviving spouse) as the beneficiary of the
Participant's interest under the Plan and who is the designated beneficiary under
Section 401(a)(9) of the Code and Treas. Reg. §1.401(a)(9)-4.

Appendix 3
TARGET BENEFIT CONTRIBUTION AND DEFINED CONTRIBUTION
ALLOCATION PROCESS
Section 1. Introduction.

This Appendix 3 describes the assumptions and methodology used to
determine the allocation of the Target Benefit Contributions and Defined
Contributions made to the Plan pursuant to Section 4.5.

Section 2. Definitions.

In addition to the definitions in Article 2, the following definitions shall apply
for purposes of this Appendix 3.

Actual Contribution Percentage: The contribution percentage determined
pursuant to Section 3(h)3) of this Appendix 3.

Active Pilot: A Group A Participant or Group B Participant who is listed on
the System Seniority List as of the Current Valuation Date.

Contribution Period: Each Plan Year shall contain two Contribution Periods:
one period from January 1 though June 30 of such Plan Year and a second period
from July 1 thorough December 31 of such Plan Year.

Current Valuation Date: The January 1 or July 1 of the Contribution Period
for which the Actual Contribution Percentage is being determined.

Frozen Pension Amount: The accrued benefit for a Group B Participant
under the Frozen Plan as of December 31, 2007 and payable at Retirement Age.

Frozen Plan: The Retirement Plan for Pilots of Hawaiian Airlines, Inc. in :
effect as of June 2, 2005.

Future Annual Pay: The annual equivalent of the Group B Participant's
Future Hourly Pay Rate assuming such Pilot works 85 hours per month.

Future Annual Average Pay: The highest consecutive 36 months of Future
Annual Pay divided by 12.

Future Hourly Pay Rate: The hourly pay rate determined pursuant to
Section 3(b) of this Appendix 3.

Future Valuation Date: Any January 1 or July 1 for any year after the
current Contribution Period.

Section 3. Methods.

(a) Seat Projection Assignment Model (SPAM).

(1) As of the Current Valuation Date, the Employer shall provide the
following information for all Active Pilots: Seat Assignment (Actual), Seat
Assignment (Highest), and Seniority Service.

(2) SPAM shall determine each Group B Participant's Seat Assignment
(Highest) for each Future Valuation Date from the Current Valuation Date through
his Retirement Age. This is accomplished by incrementally increasing the
Valuation Age and Seniority Service by six months for each Future Valuation Date
and determining for each Group B Participant, the seat he would be assigned,
assuming each Group B Participant would move to the next higher seat as that
seat becomes available due to assumed retirements.

(3) As of any Future Valuation Date, SPAM shall assume that the
distribution of WB Captains, NB Captains, WB First Officers, and NB First Officers
remains unchanged from the distribution on the Current Valuation Date. In no
event shall the seat assigned to any Group B Participant as of any Future
Valuation Date be of Seat Assignment Order lower than the Seat Assignment
(Highest) as of the Current Valuation Date.

(4) SPAM shall assign seats and determine pay for each Group B
Participant for each Future Valuation Date as follows:

Step 1: The Total Pilot Group Count shall first be compared with the
WB Captain Count. If the TPGC is greater than or equal to the WB Captain
Count, then the Active Pilots with the longest Projected Seniority Service shall be
assumed to be WB Captains (up to a maximum of the WB Captain Count). If the
TPGC is less than the WB Captain Count, then all Group B Participants shall be
assumed to be WB Captains.

Step 2: Next, the excess of the TPGC over the WB Captain Count
shall be compared with the NB Captain Count. If the excess is greater than or
equal to the NB Captain Count, then the Active Pilots with the longest Projected
Seniority Service (excluding those already assigned to a higher seat) shall be
assumed to be NB Captains up to a maximum of the NB Captain Count. If the

4

excess is less than the NB Captain Count, then all Group B Participants not
assigned in Step 1 shall be assumed to be NB Captains.

Step 3: Next, the excess of the TPGC over the WB Captain Count
and the NB Captain Count shall be compared with the WB First Officer Count. If
the excess is greater than or equal to the WB First Officer Count, then the Active
Pilots with the longest Projected Seniority Service (excluding those already
assigned to a higher seat) shall be assumed to be WB First Officers up to a
maximum of the WB First Officer Count. If the excess is less than the WB First
Officer Count, then all Group B Participants not assigned in Steps 1 or 2 shall be

: assumed to be WB First Officers.

Step 4: Finally, the excess of the TPGC over the WB Captain
Count, the NB Captain Count, and the WB First Officer Count shall be assumed to
be NB First Officers.

(b) Determination of Future Hourly Pay Rate. Each Group B Participant's
Future Hourly Pay Rate as of each Future Valuation Date shall be assigned based
on the Seat Assignment (Highest), Projected Seniority Service, and the Valuation
Hourly Pay Rate.

(c) Calculation of Future Annual Average Pay. As of the Current Valuation
Date, each Group B Participant’s Future Annual Average Pay shall be calculated.
In the year in which a Group B Participant retires, the Future Annual Pay for such
year shall be pro-rated based on the number of completed months prior to
Retirement Age.

(d) Calculation of Present Value of Future Pay. For each Group B
Participant, Present Value of Future Pay shall be calculated as the discounted
value (using only the Preretirement Interest Rate specified in Section 4 of this
Appendix 3) of Future Annual Pay assuming such pay for a Contribution Period is
received in the middle of such Contribution Period. For PVFP purposes, the
Future Annual Pay shall be calculated assuming each Group B Participant works
83 hours per month. For the Contribution Period in which a Group B Participant
attains Retirement Age, Future Annual Pay shail be pro-rated based on the
number of completed months prior to such Retirement Age.

(e) Calculation of Retirement Age Target Benefit Accumulation. For each
Group B Participant, the Projected Pension Amount shall be calculated using
Future Annual Average Pay and expected service at Retirement Age. The Target
Benefit Accumulation shall be the lump sum equivalent at Retirement Age of the
excess of this Projected Pension Amount over the Frozen Pension Amount using
the assumptions for Post-Retirement Interest, Marital Status, Form of Benefit
Payout, and Mortality specified in Section 4 of this Appendix 3.

(f) Calculation of Target Benefit Contribution and Defined Contribution
Amounts. The Target Benefit Contrioution amount for each month during a
Contribution Period shall be determined as soon as practicable after the last day of
such month as.17% of the aggregate Compensation of all Group B Participants
during such month. The Defined Contribution amount for each month during a
Contribution Period shall be determined as soon as practicable after the last day of
such month as 15% of the aggregate Compensation of all Group C Participants
during such month.

(qg) Calculation of Preliminary Target Benefit Percentage. As of the Current
Valuation Date, each Group B Participant's Preliminary Target Benefit Percentage
for the current Contribution Period is calculated as the ratio of A divided by B
where:

Ais the excess of the present value of the Target Benefit
Accumulation (using the Pre-Retirement Interest Rate specified in
Section 4 hereof only) minus the Notional Account and

B is the Present Value of Future Pay for each Group B Participant.

(h) Allocation of Target Benefit Contribution and Defined Contribution
Amounts.

(1) For each Contribution Period, the Preliminary Target Benefit
Percentage for each Group B Participant and the Preliminary Defined Contribution
Percentage for each Group C Participant shall be adjusted up or down in order to
bring the aggregate projected Employer contributions to Group B Participants and
Group C Participants within the limits specified in Section 3(f) of this Appendix 3.
This adjustment shall be the ratio that the total preliminary projected aggregate
contributions resulting from such percentages is to the total preliminary projected
contribution amounts resulting from the limits specified in Section 3(f) of this
Appendix 3.

(2) For each Contribution Period, the Preliminary Target Benefit
Percentages for Group B Participants as adjusted pursuant to Section 3(h)(1) of
this Appendix 3 shall then be adjusted to narrow the distribution of individual
percentages around the mean, but with the aggregate Employer contribution
amounts resulting therefrom the same as prior to such adjustment.

(3) The Preliminary Target Benefit Percentage for each Group B
Participant as adjusted pursuant to Section 3(h)(1) and Section 3(h)(2) of this
Appendix 3 and the Preliminary Defined Contribution Percentage for each Group B
Participant as adjusted pursuant to Section 3(h)(1) of this Appendix 3 shall be such
Participant’s Actual Contribution Percentage for such Contribution Period.

(4) For each month during such Contribution Period, each Group B
Participant's actual Target Benefit Contribution amount and each Group C
Participant's actual Defined Contribution amount shall be determined by
multiplying the product of such Pilot's Actual Contribution Percentage and his
Compensation for the month by the “Adjustment Factor” for such month.

The Adjustment Factor shail be calculated as follows:
Sum of 17% times each Group B Participant's Compensation for the
month + Sum of 15% times each Group C Participant's

Sum of each Group B Participant’s and Group C Participant’s Actual

Aggregate target contribution
Actual Employer contribution + Aggregate target contribution =
Adjustment Factor

The Adjustment Factor for a month shall be applied as follows:
Group B Participant's or Group C Participant's Actual Contribution
Percentage x his Compensation * the Adjustment Factor = the
required Employer contribution for such Participant for such month

(5) Such allocations shall be subject to the limitations of Sections
401(a)(17) and 415 of the Code. In no case shall the aggregate amount of Target
Benefit Contributions and Defined Contributions for a Plan Year exceed the
amount deductible under Section 404 of the Code. If the amount of Target Benefit
Contributions and Defined Contributions are reduced pursuant to the prior
sentence, each Group B Participant’s Target Benefit Contribution amount and
each Group C Participant's Defined Contribution amount shall be proportionately
reduced, and such reduced amount allocated in the following Plan Year.

(i) Notional Accounts and Calculation of Hypothetical Target Benefit
Contribution Amount.

(1) After the Actual Contribution Percentages for a month have been
determined pursuant to Section 3(h) of this Appendix 3, such Actual Contribution
Percentage multiplied by the Adjustment Factor for each Group B Participant shall
be used to determine the Hypothetical Target Benefit Contribution Amount to be
added to his Notional Account. This Hypothetical Target Benefit Contribution
Amount shall be based on 83 hours per month. For a Group B Participant whose ;
Seat Assignment (Actual) is the same as the Seat Assignment (Highest), the
Hypothetical Target Benefit Contribution Amount shall use the Valuation Pay

determined by his Seat Assignment (Actual). For a Group B Participant whose
Seat Assignment (Actual) is not the same as the Seat Assignment (Highest), the
Hypothetical Target Benefit Contribution Amount shall use the Valuation Pay
expected to be received by such Participant for the Contribution Period.
(2) A Group B Participant's Hypothetical Target Benefit Contribution

Amount for a month shall be compounded by the Pre-Retirement Interest Rate
specified in Section 4 of this Appendix 3 and then added to his Notional Account.

(i) Special rule for Group B Participants recalled from furlough or returning
from leave of absence during a Contribution Period. If a Participant is recalled

and shall be adjusted during such Contribution Period in accordance with Section

Section 4. Assumptions.

The following assumptions shall apply for purposes of this Appendix 3:

Form of Payment under the Frozen Plan: Projected Pension Amount

assumed to be paid as a Joint & 50% Survivor Annuity.

Marital Status: All Pilots assumed to be married at Retirement Age with a

spouse 4 years younger.

(50/50 blend), projected with Scale AA to 2002.

Pay Scale Adjustment Factor: 1% compounded annually.

Pre-Retirement Decrements: None.

Pre-Retirement Interest Rate: 8% compounded annually.

Post-Retirement Interest Rate: 7.25% compounded annually.

deny the Participant's application for Benefits under the Plan. The Retirement Board

Exhibit 1
A compounded average rate of return for the S&P 500 Index Fund will be used to
calculate earnings on the contributions. Under this method, the rate of return for the S&P 500
Index Fund will first be determined for each year or portion of a year (hereinafter “Period”).
The aggregate amounts of the contributions for each Period will be assumed to be made

at the mid-point of such Period. Such contributions will initially earn one-half of the rate of
return of the Period. In the following Period, the previously-made contributions will earn the
rate of return for the S&P 500 Index Fund for the whole Period, on a compounded basis.

Example: If for Period 1 the contribution for Participant A is $100 and the rate of

return in Period 1 is 10%, the earnings credit for the contribution for Period 1 will

be $5.00, calculated as follows:

$100.00 x 10% x 50% = $5.00

Thus the value of the contribution and the earnings credit at the end of Period 1

would total $105.

If for Period 2 the contribution for Participant A is $150 and the rate of return for

the S&P 500 Index Fund in Period 2 is 14%, the earnings credit for the

contributions for Periods 1 and 2 will be calculated as follows:

($105.00 x 14%) + (150.00 x 14% x 50%) = $14.70 + $10.50 = $25.20
The value of the contributions and the earnings credit at the end of the Period 2
would total $280.20 ($105.00 + $150.00 +25.20).
